translations.literal: Volume 132
translations.idiomatic: Volume 132

sentences.zh: 【宋紀十四】 起強圉協洽，盡上章閹茂，凡四年。

translations.literal: [Song Records 14] Beginning in Qiangyu Xieqia, ending in Shangzhang Yanmao, four years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Song Records 14] From Qiangyu Xieqia through Shangzhang Yanmao—four years in all.

sentences.zh: 太宗明皇帝中泰始三年（

translations.literal: Third year of Taishi of Emperor Ming of Northern Wei (
translations.idiomatic: Third year of the Taishi reign of Emperor Ming of Northern Wei (

sentences.zh: 丁未，公元四六七年）

translations.literal: dingwei, CE 467)
translations.idiomatic: dingwei, 467 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，張永等棄城夜遁。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Zhang Yong and others abandoned the city and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Zhang Yong and his colleagues abandoned the city and fled under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 會天大雪，泗水冰合，永等棄船步走，士卒凍死者太半，手足斷者什七八。

translations.literal: It happened that heaven sent great snow; the Si River froze solid. Yong and the others abandoned their boats and went on foot; more than half the soldiers died of cold, and seven or eight in ten suffered severed hands or feet.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy snow fell, the Si froze over, and Yong's men left their ships to march on foot. More than half the troops froze to death, and seven or eight in ten lost hands or feet to the cold.

sentences.zh: 尉元邀其前，薛安都乘其後，大破永等於呂梁之東，死者以萬數，枕屍六十餘里，委棄軍資器械不可勝計；

translations.literal: Wei Yuan intercepted them in front; Xue Andu struck from behind and utterly defeated Yong and the others east of Lüliang. The dead numbered in the tens of thousands; corpses lay piled for more than sixty li; abandoned military stores and weapons were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yuan blocked their path ahead while Xue Andu hit them from the rear and routed them east of Lüliang. Tens of thousands were killed, the dead lay heaped for more than sixty li, and abandoned supplies and arms were beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 永足指亦墮，與沈攸之僅以身免，梁、南秦二州刺史垣恭祖等為魏所虜。

translations.literal: Yong's toes also fell off; he and Shen Youzhi barely escaped with their lives. Yuan Gongzu, regional inspector of Liang and Southern Qin, and others were captured by Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yong lost his toes as well; he and Shen Youzhi barely got away alive. Yuan Gongzu, inspector of Liang and Southern Qin, and others were taken prisoner by Wei.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，召蔡興宗，以敗書示之，曰：「我愧卿甚！」

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it, he summoned Cai Xingzong, showed him the report of defeat, and said, "I am deeply ashamed before you!"
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard the news, he summoned Cai Xingzong, showed him the defeat report, and said, "I have failed you badly!"

sentences.zh: 永降號左將軍；

translations.literal: Yong was demoted in rank to Left General;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yong was reduced in rank to Left General;

sentences.zh: 攸之免官，以貞陽公領職還屯淮陰。

translations.literal: Youzhi was removed from office; as Duke of Zhenyang he retained his post and returned to garrison Huaiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi was dismissed from office but kept his duties as Duke of Zhenyang and withdrew to camp at Huaiyin.

sentences.zh: 由是失淮北四州及豫州淮西之地。

translations.literal: Because of this they lost the four provinces north of the Huai and the lands west of the Huai in Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: As a result the Song lost the four prefectures north of the Huai and the Huai-western districts of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 裴子野論曰：昔齊桓矜於葵丘而九國叛，曹公不禮張松而天下分。

translations.literal: Pei Ziye commented: In old times Duke Huan of Qi grew arrogant at Kuiqiu and the nine states rebelled; Lord Cao treated Zhang Song without courtesy and the realm split apart.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ziye wrote: Once Duke Huan of Qi grew arrogant at Kuiqiu and the nine states turned against him; Cao Cao slighted Zhang Song and the empire broke apart.

sentences.zh: 一失毫釐，其差遠矣。

translations.literal: One slip of a hair's breadth, and the deviation is vast.
translations.idiomatic: A single misstep no wider than a hair, and the consequences stretch far indeed.

sentences.zh: 太宗之初，威令所被，不滿百里，卒有離心，士無固色，而能開誠心，布款實，莫不感恩服德，致命效死，故西摧北蕩，寓內褰開。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Taizong, the reach of his authority and commands was less than a hundred li; the soldiers had divided hearts and the officers had no firm resolve. Yet he could open his sincere heart and spread genuine good faith, so that none failed to feel gratitude and submit to his virtue, giving their lives in loyal service—therefore he crushed the west and swept the north, and within the realm barriers were thrown open.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset Taizong's authority extended less than a hundred li; troops were divided in loyalty and officers lacked firm resolve. Yet by opening his heart and dealing in good faith he won such gratitude and willing service that men gave their lives for him—westward he broke his foes, northward he swept them aside, and the heartland opened before him.

sentences.zh: 既而六軍獻捷，方隅束手，天子欲賈其餘威，師出無名，長淮以北，倏忽為戎。

translations.literal: Thereafter the six armies presented victories and the corners of the realm were helpless; the Son of Heaven wished to trade on his remaining prestige, but the army marched out without a righteous name, and north of the Long Huai, in a flash, became barbarian land.
translations.idiomatic: Then his armies brought repeated victories and the borderlands were at his mercy; the emperor sought to spend his remaining prestige, but campaigns launched without just cause turned everything north of the Huai, in an instant, into enemy territory.

sentences.zh: 惜乎！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: What a pity!

sentences.zh: 若以向之虛懷，不驕不伐，則三叛奚為而起哉！

translations.literal: If he had kept his former open-mindedness, neither proud nor boastful, then why would the three rebellions have arisen!
translations.idiomatic: Had he kept his earlier humility, free of pride and boasting, what cause would the three rebellions have had to rise!

sentences.zh: 高祖蟣虱生介冑，經啟疆場；

translations.literal: The High Ancestor, with lice born in his armor, opened and secured the borders;
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor wore lice in his mail as he carved out the realm;

sentences.zh: 後之子孫，日蹙百里。

translations.literal: his later descendants daily shrink a hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: yet his descendants now lose a hundred li a day.

sentences.zh: 播獲堂構，豈雲易哉！

translations.literal: To sow and reap while building the hall—can it be called easy!
translations.idiomatic: To win an empire in battle and then hold it in peace—how can that be easy!

sentences.zh: 魏尉元以彭城兵荒之後，公私困竭，請發冀、相、濟、兗四州粟，取張永所棄船九百艘，沿清運載，以賑新民；

translations.literal: Wei Yuan of Wei, because after the war and famine at Pengcheng public and private resources were exhausted, requested that grain be sent from the four provinces Ji, Xiang, Ji, and Yan, and that the nine hundred boats abandoned by Zhang Yong be taken and used to transport it along the Qing River to relieve the new subjects.
translations.idiomatic: After war and famine had drained Pengcheng, Wei's Wei Yuan asked that grain be levied from Ji, Xiang, Ji, and Yan, that Zhang Yong's nine hundred abandoned ships be used to haul it down the Qing, and that the supplies be used to succor the newly submitted population.

sentences.zh: 魏朝從之。

translations.literal: The Wei court followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei court approved his plan.

sentences.zh: 魏東平王道符反於長安，殺副將駙馬都尉萬古真等；

translations.literal: Wei's Prince of Dongping, Daofu, rebelled at Chang'an and killed the deputy commander, Commandant of the Horse for the Imperial Son-in-Law, Wan Guzhen, and others;
translations.idiomatic: Wei's Prince of Dongping, Daofu, rose in rebellion at Chang'an and killed the deputy commander, Commandant of the Horse for the Imperial Son-in-Law Wan Guzhen, and others;

sentences.zh: 丙午，司空和其奴等將殿中兵討之。

translations.literal: On bingwu, the Minister of Works He Qinu and others led the Palace Army to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu the Minister of Works He Qinu and others marched with the Palace Army to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 丁未，道符司馬段太陽攻道符，斬之；

translations.literal: On dingwei, Daofu's Major Duan Taiyang attacked Daofu and beheaded him;
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei Daofu's major Duan Taiyang attacked him and cut off his head;

sentences.zh: 以安西將軍陸真為長安鎮將以撫之。

translations.literal: the General Who Pacifies the West Lu Zhen was made garrison commander of Chang'an to pacify the region.
translations.idiomatic: and General Who Pacifies the West Lu Zhen was appointed garrison commander of Chang'an to restore order.

sentences.zh: 道符，翰之子也。

translations.literal: Daofu was the son of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Daofu was a son of Han.

sentences.zh: 閏月，魏以頓丘王李峻為太宰。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, Wei appointed Prince of Dunqiu Li Jun as Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month Wei appointed Prince of Dunqiu Li Jun Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 沈文秀、崔道固為土人所攻，遣使乞降於魏，且請兵自救。

translations.literal: Shen Wenxiu and Cui Daogu were attacked by the local people; they sent envoys to beg surrender to Wei and also requested troops to save themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Under attack by local forces, Shen Wenxiu and Cui Daogu sent envoys to offer surrender to Wei and to ask for troops to rescue them.

sentences.zh: 二月，魏西河公石自懸瓠引兵攻汝陰太守張超，不克；

translations.literal: In the second month, Wei's Duke of Xihe, Shi, led troops from Xuanhu to attack Zhang Chao, administrator of Ruyin, but could not take it;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Wei's Duke of Xihe, Shi, marched from Xuanhu against Zhang Chao, administrator of Ruyin, but failed to capture the city;

sentences.zh: 退屯陳項，議還長社，待秋擊之。

translations.literal: he withdrew to camp at Chenxiang and discussed returning to Changshe to wait until autumn to attack.
translations.idiomatic: he withdrew to Chenxiang and proposed returning to Changshe to wait until autumn before striking again.

sentences.zh: 鄭羲曰：「張超蟻聚窮命，糧食已盡，不降當走，可翹足而待也。

translations.literal: Zheng Xi said, "Zhang Chao is like ants gathered at the end of their fate; their grain is already exhausted. If they do not surrender they will flee—we can wait with foot raised.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xi said, "Zhang Chao is cornered like ants in a nest; his grain is gone. If he does not surrender he will run—we need only wait with folded arms.

sentences.zh: 今棄之遠去，超修城浚隍，積薪儲谷，更來恐難圖矣。」

translations.literal: Now if we abandon them and go far away, Chao will repair the walls, deepen the moat, pile firewood and store grain, and when we come again I fear he will be hard to deal with."
translations.idiomatic: If we leave him now, Chao will repair his walls, deepen his moat, and stock fuel and grain—and when we return he will be far harder to take."

sentences.zh: 石不從，遂還長社。

translations.literal: Shi did not follow this and therefore returned to Changshe.
translations.idiomatic: Shi refused and marched back to Changshe.

sentences.zh: 初，尋陽既平，帝遣沈文秀弟文炳以詔書諭文秀，又遣輔國將軍劉懷珍將馬步三千人與文炳偕行。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Xunyang was pacified, the emperor sent Shen Wenxiu's younger brother Wenbing with an imperial edict to instruct Wenxiu, and also sent the General Who Assists the State Liu Huaizhen with three thousand horse and foot to go together with Wenbing.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Xunyang had been pacified, the emperor sent Shen Wenxiu's younger brother Wenbing with an edict to reason with him, and dispatched General Who Assists the State Liu Huaizhen with three thousand cavalry and infantry to accompany Wenbing.

sentences.zh: 未至，值張永等敗退，懷珍還鎮山陽。

translations.literal: Before they arrived, Zhang Yong and others were defeated and retreated; Huaizhen returned to garrison Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Before they arrived, Zhang Yong's army was beaten and driven back, and Huaizhen returned to his post at Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 文秀攻青州刺史明僧暠，帝使懷珍帥龍驤將軍王廣之將五百騎、步卒二千人浮海救之，至東海，僧暠已退保東萊。

translations.literal: Wenxiu attacked Ming Seng'ao, regional inspector of Qingzhou; the emperor had Huaizhen lead the Dragon Cavalry General Wang Guangzhi with five hundred horsemen and two thousand foot soldiers by sea to rescue him. When they reached Donghai, Seng'ao had already withdrawn to defend Donglai.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenxiu attacked Qingzhou inspector Ming Seng'ao, the emperor ordered Huaizhen, with Dragon Cavalry General Wang Guangzhi and five hundred horse plus two thousand foot, to sail to his relief; by the time they reached Donghai, Seng'ao had already fallen back to Donglai.

sentences.zh: 懷珍進據朐城，眾心兇懼，欲且保郁洲，懷珍曰：「文秀欲以青州歸索虜，計齊之士民，安肯甘心左衽邪！

translations.literal: Huaizhen advanced and occupied Qucheng; the hearts of the masses were fearful and they wished for the time being to hold Yuzhou. Huaizhen said, "Wenxiu wishes to give Qingzhou to the northern barbarians—I reckon the gentry and common people of Qi, how could they willingly accept the left lapel!
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhen advanced and seized Qucheng, but his men were afraid and wanted to fall back to Yuzhou. He said, "Wenxiu means to hand Qingzhou to the northern invaders—do you think the people of Qi will willingly wear barbarian dress!

sentences.zh: 今揚兵直前，宣佈威德，諸城可飛書而下。

translations.literal: Now if we raise our banners and go straight forward, proclaiming our might and virtue, the various cities can be taken by a flying letter.
translations.idiomatic: March straight ahead, proclaim our power and justice, and the cities will surrender at the first message we send.

sentences.zh: 奈何守此不進，自為沮撓乎！」

translations.literal: Why hold here and not advance, discouraging ourselves!"
translations.idiomatic: Why sit here and hold ourselves back!"

sentences.zh: 遂進，至黔陬，文秀所署高密、平昌二郡太守棄城走。

translations.literal: Thereupon he advanced to Qianzou; the administrators of Gaomi and Pingchang, two commanderies appointed by Wenxiu, abandoned their cities and fled.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed on to Qianzou, and the Gaomi and Pingchang prefects Wenxiu had appointed abandoned their cities and fled.

sentences.zh: 懷珍送致文炳，達朝廷意，文秀猶不降；

translations.literal: Huaizhen sent Wenbing forward to convey the court's intent, but Wenxiu still would not surrender;
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhen sent Wenbing ahead to deliver the court's message, yet Wenxiu still refused to submit;

sentences.zh: 百姓聞懷珍至，皆喜。

translations.literal: when the common people heard that Huaizhen had come, all were pleased.
translations.idiomatic: but when the people heard Huaizhen had arrived, they rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 文秀所署長廣太守劉桃根將數千人戍不其城。

translations.literal: Liu Taogen, administrator of Changguang appointed by Wenxiu, led several thousand men to garrison Bucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Taogen, Wenxiu's appointee as administrator of Changguang, held Bucheng with several thousand men.

sentences.zh: 懷珍軍於洋水，眾謂且宜堅壁伺隙，懷珍曰：「今眾少糧竭，懸軍深入，正當以精兵速進，掩其不備耳。」

translations.literal: Huaizhen encamped on the Yang River; the masses said they should for the time being strengthen the walls and watch for an opening. Huaizhen said, "Now our numbers are few and grain exhausted; we are a lone army deep in enemy country—we should use picked troops to advance swiftly and strike them unprepared."
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhen camped on the Yang River; his officers urged him to stand on the defensive and wait for an opening. He said, "We are few, our grain is gone, and we are deep in hostile country—the only course is to strike fast with elite troops while they are off guard."

sentences.zh: 乃遣王廣之將百騎襲不其城，拔之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent Wang Guangzhi with a hundred horsemen to raid Bucheng and took it.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Wang Guangzhi with a hundred horse to storm Bucheng and captured it.

sentences.zh: 文秀聞諸城皆敗，乃遣使請降；

translations.literal: When Wenxiu heard that all the cities had been defeated, he then sent envoys to request surrender;
translations.idiomatic: When Wenxiu learned that his outposts had fallen, he sent envoys to offer surrender;

sentences.zh: 帝復以為青州刺史。

translations.literal: the emperor again appointed him regional inspector of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: and the emperor restored him as inspector of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 崔道固亦請降，復以為冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Cui Daogu also requested surrender and was again made regional inspector of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Daogu submitted as well and was reappointed inspector of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 懷珍引還。

translations.literal: Huaizhen led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhen then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 魏濟陰王小新成卒。

translations.literal: Wei's Prince of Jiyin, Xiaoxincheng, died.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoxincheng, Prince of Jiyin of Wei, died.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之之自彭城還也，留長水校尉王玄載守下邳，積射將軍沈韶守宿豫，睢陵、淮陽皆留兵戌之。

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi returned from Pengcheng, he left the Chief Commandant of the Chang River Wang Xuanzai to guard Xiapi, the General of Accumulated Archery Shen Shao to guard Suyu, and stationed troops at Suiling and Huaiyang as well.
translations.idiomatic: On his return from Pengcheng, Shen Youzhi left Chief Commandant of the Chang River Wang Xuanzai at Xiapi, General of Accumulated Archery Shen Shao at Suyu, and garrisons at Suiling and Huaiyang.

sentences.zh: 玄載，玄謨之從弟也。

translations.literal: Xuanzai was a younger cousin of Xuanmo.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzai was a younger cousin of Wang Xuanmo.

sentences.zh: 時東平太守申纂守無鹽，幽州刺史劉休賓守梁鄒，并州刺史清河房崇吉守升城，輔國將軍清河張讜守團城，及兗州刺史王整、蘭陵太守桓忻、肥城、糜溝、垣苗等戍皆不附於魏。

translations.literal: At this time the Administrator of Dongping Shen Zuan held Wuyan; Liu Xiubin, regional inspector of Youzhou, held Liangzou; Fang Chongji of Qinghe, regional inspector of Bingzhou, held Shengcheng; Zhang Dan of Qinghe, General Who Assists the State, held Tuancheng; and the regional inspector of Yanzhou Wang Zheng, the administrator of Lanling Huan Xin, and the garrisons at Feicheng, Migou, and Yuan Miao and others all did not submit to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Zuan, administrator of Dongping, held Wuyan; Liu Xiubin of Youzhou held Liangzou; Bingzhou inspector Fang Chongji of Qinghe held Shengcheng; Zhang Dan of Qinghe, General Who Assists the State, held Tuancheng; and Yanzhou inspector Wang Zheng, Lanling administrator Huan Xin, and the garrisons at Feicheng, Migou, Yuan Miao, and elsewhere still refused to submit to Wei.

sentences.zh: 休賓，乘民之兄子也。

translations.literal: Xiubin was the nephew of Chengmin.
translations.idiomatic: Xiubin was a nephew of Liu Chengmin.

sentences.zh: 魏遣平東將軍長孫陵等將兵赴青州，征南大將軍慕容白曜將騎五萬為之繼援。

translations.literal: Wei sent the General Who Pacifies the East Changsun Ling and others to lead troops to Qingzhou; the General-in-Chief Who Conquers the South Murong Baiyao led fifty thousand cavalry as follow-up support.
translations.idiomatic: Wei dispatched General Who Pacifies the East Changsun Ling and others toward Qingzhou, with General-in-Chief Who Conquers the South Murong Baiyao and fifty thousand horse as reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 白曜，燕太祖之玄孫也。

translations.literal: Baiyao was a great-great-grandson of Yan's founding emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao was a great-great-grandson of the founding emperor of Yan.

sentences.zh: 白曜至無鹽，欲攻之。

translations.literal: When Baiyao reached Wuyan, he wished to attack it.
translations.idiomatic: When Baiyao reached Wuyan he intended to assault it at once.

sentences.zh: 將佐皆以為攻具未備，不宜遽進。

translations.literal: The generals and assistants all thought the siege equipment was not ready and that they should not advance hastily.
translations.idiomatic: His officers argued that siege equipment was not ready and that a hasty advance was unwise.

sentences.zh: 左司馬范陽酈范曰：「今輕軍遠襲，深入敵境，豈宜淹緩！

translations.literal: The Left Major of the Army, Li Fan of Fanyang, said, "Now we are a light army on a distant raid deep in enemy territory—how can we afford to delay!
translations.idiomatic: Left Major Li Fan of Fanyang said, "We are a light force on a deep raid into enemy country—how can we afford to linger!

sentences.zh: 且申纂必謂我軍來速，不暇攻圍，將不為備；

translations.literal: Moreover Shen Zuan will surely think our army comes quickly and has no time to besiege, and will not make preparations;
translations.idiomatic: Shen Zuan will assume we came too fast to mount a siege and will leave his defenses slack;

sentences.zh: 今若出其不意，可一鼓而克。」

translations.literal: if now we strike with unexpected speed, we can take it in one drumbeat."
translations.idiomatic: strike now by surprise and we can take the city in a single assault."

sentences.zh: 白曜曰：「司馬策是也。」

translations.literal: Baiyao said, "The Major's plan is right."
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao said, "The Major is right."

sentences.zh: 乃引兵偽退。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led the army in a feigned retreat.
translations.idiomatic: He marched away as if in retreat.

sentences.zh: 申纂不復設備，白曜夜中部分，三月，甲寅旦，攻城，食時，克之；

translations.literal: Shen Zuan no longer made preparations; Baiyao in the middle of the night divided his forces. In the third month, on jiayin at dawn, he attacked the city; by mealtime he had taken it;
translations.idiomatic: Zuan let his guard down. Baiyao divided his forces in the night; on jiayin at dawn in the third month he assaulted the walls and had the city by midmorning;

sentences.zh: 纂走，追擒，殺之。

translations.literal: Zuan fled; they pursued, captured, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan fled, was overtaken, captured, and executed.

sentences.zh: 白曜欲盡以無鹽人為軍賞，酈范曰：「齊，形勝之地，宜遠為經略。

translations.literal: Baiyao wished to give all the people of Wuyan as military rewards. Li Fan said, "Qi is a land of strategic advantage; one should plan for it from afar.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao wanted to hand over the entire population of Wuyan as booty to his troops. Li Fan said, "Qi is a land of strategic strength; we must think in terms of long-term conquest.

sentences.zh: 今王師始入其境，人心未洽，連城相望，鹹有拒守之志，苟非以德信懷之，未易平也。」

translations.literal: Now the royal army has only just entered its borders; hearts are not yet united; linked cities face one another, all with the will to resist and hold. If we do not win them with virtue and good faith, it will not be easy to pacify."
translations.idiomatic: Our army has only just entered; the people are not yet won over; city after city still means to resist. Unless we win them with virtue and trust, pacification will not come easily."

sentences.zh: 白曜曰：「善！」

translations.literal: Baiyao said, "Good!"
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao said, "Well said!"

sentences.zh: 皆免之。

translations.literal: He pardoned them all.
translations.idiomatic: He spared them all.

sentences.zh: 白曜將攻肥城，酈范曰：「肥城雖小，攻之引日，勝之不能益軍勢，不勝足以挫軍威。

translations.literal: Baiyao was about to attack Feicheng. Li Fan said, "Though Feicheng is small, attacking it will draw out days; if victorious it cannot increase the army's momentum, and if not victorious it is enough to damage the army's prestige.
translations.idiomatic: As Baiyao prepared to attack Feicheng, Li Fan said, "Feicheng is small, but a siege will drag on; victory there will not strengthen our momentum, and defeat would shame the army.

sentences.zh: 彼見無鹽之破，死傷塗地，不敢不懼；

translations.literal: When they see the fall of Wuyan, the dead and wounded covering the ground, they will not dare fail to fear;
translations.idiomatic: They have seen Wuyan fall and the ground strewn with dead—they will be terrified;

sentences.zh: 若飛書告諭，縱使不降，亦當逃散。」

translations.literal: if we send a flying letter to announce and instruct them, even if they do not surrender they should scatter and flee."
translations.idiomatic: send a proclamation and even if they do not surrender they will flee."

sentences.zh: 白曜從之，肥城果潰，獲粟三十萬斛。

translations.literal: Baiyao followed this; Feicheng indeed collapsed, and they obtained three hundred thousand hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao took his advice; Feicheng collapsed, and they seized three hundred thousand hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 白曜謂范曰：「此行得卿，三齊不足定也。」

translations.literal: Baiyao said to Fan, "On this campaign, having obtained you, the Three Qi are not enough to be hard to settle."
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao told Fan, "With you on this campaign, the Three Qi will not be hard to subdue."

sentences.zh: 遂取垣苗、麋溝二戍。

translations.literal: Thereupon he took the two garrisons of Yuan Miao and Migou.
translations.idiomatic: He then took the garrisons at Yuan Miao and Migou.

sentences.zh: 一旬中連拔四城，威震齊土。

translations.literal: Within ten days he captured four cities in succession, and his prestige shook the land of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days he captured four cities in a row, and his fame shook all Qi.

sentences.zh: 丙子，以尚書左僕射蔡興守為郢州刺史。

translations.literal: On bingzi, Cai Xingshou, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was made regional inspector of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi Cai Xingshou, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was appointed inspector of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 房崇吉守升城，勝兵者不過七百人。

translations.literal: Fang Chongji held Shengcheng; his effective soldiers were no more than seven hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Chongji defended Shengcheng with no more than seven hundred fit troops.

sentences.zh: 慕容白曜築長圍以攻之，自二月至於夏四月，乃克之。

translations.literal: Murong Baiyao built a long encirclement to attack it; from the second month until the fourth month of summer he then took it.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Baiyao invested it with a long siege; from the second month until the fourth month of summer he finally took the city.

sentences.zh: 白曜忿其不降，欲盡坑城中人，參軍事昌黎韓麒麟諫曰：「今勍敵在前而坑其民，自此以東，諸城人自為守，不可克也。

translations.literal: Baiyao resented that they had not surrendered and wished to bury alive all the people in the city. The staff officer Han Qilin of Changli remonstrated, saying, "Now with fierce enemies in front, if we bury the people alive, from here eastward the people of the various cities will defend themselves on their own and cannot be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Angry at their refusal to submit, Baiyao meant to slaughter every soul in the city. Staff officer Han Qilin of Changli objected: "With strong foes still ahead, massacring these people will make every city east of here fight to the last man.

sentences.zh: 師老糧盡，外寇乘之，此危道也。」

translations.literal: The army grows weary and grain is exhausted; external enemies will seize the moment—this is a perilous path."
translations.idiomatic: Our army will tire, our grain run out, and outside enemies will strike—that is the road to ruin."

sentences.zh: 白曜乃慰撫其民，各使復業。

translations.literal: Baiyao thereupon comforted and soothed the people and had each return to his occupation.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao relented, comforted the people, and let them return to their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 崇吉脫身走。

translations.literal: Chongji escaped and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Chongji slipped away and escaped.

sentences.zh: 崇吉母傅氏，申纂妻賈氏，與濟州刺史盧度世有中表親，然已疏遠。

translations.literal: Chongji's mother Lady Fu, Shen Zuan's wife Lady Jia, and Lu Dushi, regional inspector of Jizhou, had ties as cousins by marriage, but they had already grown distant.
translations.idiomatic: Chongji's mother Lady Fu and Shen Zuan's wife Lady Jia were cousins by marriage of Jizhou inspector Lu Dushi, though the families had long been estranged.

sentences.zh: 及為魏所虜，度世奉事甚恭，贍給優厚。

translations.literal: When they were captured by Wei, Dushi served them very respectfully and provided support generously.
translations.idiomatic: After they were taken by Wei, Dushi treated them with great respect and supported them generously.

sentences.zh: 度世閨門之內，和而有禮。

translations.literal: Within Dushi's inner quarters there was harmony and propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Within his household harmony and courtesy prevailed.

sentences.zh: 雖世有屯夷，家有貧富，百口怡怡，豐儉同之。

translations.literal: Although in the world there were hardships and in families there were rich and poor, the hundred mouths were joyful together, sharing abundance and scarcity alike.
translations.idiomatic: Though the times were harsh and households differed in wealth, his clan of a hundred souls lived in contentment, sharing alike in plenty and want.

sentences.zh: 崔道固閉門抿魏。

translations.literal: Cui Daogu closed his gates and resisted Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Daogu shut his gates and held out against Wei.

sentences.zh: 沈文秀遣使迎降於魏，請兵援接。

translations.literal: Shen Wenxiu sent envoys to welcome surrender to Wei and requested troops for support and connection.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Wenxiu sent envoys to offer surrender to Wei and to ask for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 白曜欲遣兵赴之，酈范曰：「文秀室家墳墓皆在江南，擁兵數萬，城固甲堅。

translations.literal: Baiyao wished to send troops to go to them. Li Fan said, "Wenxiu's family and ancestral graves are all south of the Yangtze; he commands tens of thousands of troops, and his city is strong and armor firm.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao wanted to send troops to their aid. Li Fan said, "Wenxiu's family and ancestral graves lie south of the Yangtze; he commands tens of thousands of men behind strong walls and stout armor.

sentences.zh: 強則拒戰，屈則遁去。

translations.literal: When strong he resists in battle; when bent he slips away.
translations.idiomatic: While he is strong he will fight; if pressed he will flee.

sentences.zh: 我師未逼其城，無朝夕之急，何所畏忌，而遽求援軍！

translations.literal: Our army has not yet pressed his city; there is no urgency of morning and evening—what does he fear that he hastily seeks relief troops!
translations.idiomatic: Our army has not yet threatened his walls; he faces no immediate peril—what has he to fear that he rushes to beg for reinforcements!

sentences.zh: 且觀其使者，視下而色愧，語煩而志怯。

translations.literal: Moreover, observe his envoys: they look downward and their color is ashamed; their speech is verbose and their will timid.
translations.idiomatic: Watch his envoys: their eyes are downcast, their faces ashamed; their words are many and their spirit faint.

sentences.zh: 此必挾詐以誘我，不可從也。

translations.literal: This must be carrying deceit to lure us—we cannot follow it.
translations.idiomatic: This is surely a ruse to lure us—we must not heed it.

sentences.zh: 不若先取歷城，克盤陽，下梁鄒，平樂陵，然後按兵徐進，不患其不服也。」

translations.literal: Better first to take Licheng, capture Panyang, descend on Liangzou, pacify Leling, and then hold the army and advance slowly—there is no worry that they will not submit."
translations.idiomatic: Better to take Licheng first, capture Panyang, reduce Liangzou, pacify Leling, and only then advance at leisure—then we need not fear that they will refuse to submit."

sentences.zh: 白曜曰；

translations.literal: Baiyao said;
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao said,

sentences.zh: 「崔道固等兵力單弱，不敢出戰；

translations.literal: "Cui Daogu and the others have few troops and are weak; they do not dare come out to fight;
translations.idiomatic: "Cui Daogu and the rest are too weak to dare give battle;

sentences.zh: 吾通行無礙，直抵東陽，彼自知必亡，故望風求服，夫又何疑！」

translations.literal: Our passage is unimpeded; we can go straight to Dongyang. They themselves know they must perish, and therefore seek submission at the sight of our banners—what is there to doubt!"
translations.idiomatic: Our march is unblocked—we can strike straight for Dongyang. They know they are doomed and come begging at the first rumor of our approach—what is there to doubt!"

sentences.zh: 范曰：「歷城兵多糧足，非朝夕可拔。

translations.literal: Fan said, "Licheng has many troops and ample grain; it cannot be taken in a morning or evening.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fan replied, "Licheng is strong in men and grain and cannot be taken overnight.

sentences.zh: 文秀坐據東陽，為諸城根本。

translations.literal: Wenxiu sits holding Dongyang as the root of the various cities.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu holds Dongyang as the anchor of all these cities.

sentences.zh: 今多遣兵則無以攻歷城，少遣兵則不足以制東陽；

translations.literal: If we send many troops now, we will have none to attack Licheng; if we send few, they will not suffice to control Dongyang;
translations.idiomatic: Send a large force and we cannot take Licheng; send a small one and we cannot hold Dongyang in check;

sentences.zh: 若進為文秀所拒，退為諸城所邀，腹背受敵，必無全理。

translations.literal: if we advance and are rejected by Wenxiu, and retreat and are intercepted by the various cities, attacked front and rear, there will surely be no way to remain whole.
translations.idiomatic: if we advance and Wenxiu blocks us, then retreat and the other cities cut us off, we will be caught front and rear with no hope of escape.

sentences.zh: 願更審計，無墮賊彀中。」

translations.literal: I wish you would reconsider the plan and not fall into the enemy's trap."
translations.idiomatic: Please reconsider and do not walk into their trap."

sentences.zh: 白曜乃止。

translations.literal: Baiyao thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao held back.

sentences.zh: 文秀果不降。

translations.literal: Wenxiu indeed did not surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu, as Fan had predicted, did not submit.

sentences.zh: 魏尉元上表稱：「彭城賊之要籓，不有重兵積粟，則不可固守；

translations.literal: Wei Yuan of Wei submitted a memorial stating, "Pengcheng is a strategic fortress of the bandits; without heavy troops and accumulated grain it cannot be firmly held;
translations.idiomatic: Wei's Wei Yuan memorialized: "Pengcheng is the enemy's key stronghold; without a large garrison and stored grain it cannot be held;

sentences.zh: 若資儲既廣，雖劉彧師徒悉起，不敢窺淮北之地。」

translations.literal: if stores are already ample, even if Liu Yu's armies and followers all rise, they will not dare to peer at the lands north of the Huai."
translations.idiomatic: once our supplies are ample, even if Liu Yu musters every soldier he has, he will not dare look north of the Huai again."

sentences.zh: 又言：「若賊向彭城，必由清、泗過宿豫，歷下邳；

translations.literal: He also said, "If the bandits move on Pengcheng, they must pass through Suqian by way of the Qing and Si, and go by Xiapi;
translations.idiomatic: He added, "If the enemy marches on Pengcheng he must pass Suqian along the Qing and Si and come by Xiapi;

sentences.zh: 趨青州，亦由下邳、沂水經東安。

translations.literal: if they hurry to Qingzhou, they also go from Xiapi and the Yi River through Dong'an.
translations.idiomatic: and if he aims for Qingzhou he will likewise go from Xiapi along the Yi through Dong'an.

sentences.zh: 此數者，皆為賊用師之要。

translations.literal: These several routes are all essentials for the bandits' use of troops.
translations.idiomatic: All these are vital lines for the enemy's armies.

sentences.zh: 今若先定下邳，平宿豫，鎮淮陽，戍東安，則青、冀諸鎮可不攻而克；

translations.literal: Now if we first secure Xiapi, pacify Suqian, garrison Huaiyang, and defend Dong'an, then the various garrisons of Qing and Ji can be taken without attack;
translations.idiomatic: If we first take Xiapi, pacify Suqian, hold Huaiyang, and garrison Dong'an, the Qing and Ji strongholds will fall without a fight;

sentences.zh: 若四城不服，青、冀雖拔，百姓狼顧，猶懷僥倖之心。

translations.literal: if the four cities do not submit, even though Qing and Ji are taken, the common people will look back like wolves and still harbor a mind of lucky chance.
translations.idiomatic: if those four cities hold out, even after Qing and Ji are taken the people will look over their shoulders and still hope for rescue.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為，宜釋青、冀之師，先定東南之地，斷劉彧北顧之意，絕愚民南望之心；

translations.literal: Your servant foolishly thinks we should release the armies of Qing and Ji, first settle the southeast lands, cut off Liu Yu's thought of looking north, and sever the foolish people's heart of gazing south;
translations.idiomatic: I believe we should leave off Qing and Ji for now, secure the southeast first, break Liu Yu's hope of looking north, and cut off the common people's longing for the south;

sentences.zh: 夏水雖盛，無津途可由，冬路雖通，無高城可固。

translations.literal: though summer waters are swollen, there is no ford or route by which they may pass; though winter roads are open, there are no high cities to make firm.
translations.idiomatic: in summer the rivers run high and there is no crossing; in winter the roads are open but there are no strong walls to shelter them.

sentences.zh: 如此，則淮北自舉，暫勞永逸。

translations.literal: In this way the north of the Huai will raise itself, a brief toil for a lasting ease.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Huai north will submit of itself—brief effort, lasting gain.

sentences.zh: 兵貴神速，久則生變，若天雨既降，彼或因水通，運糧益眾，規為進取，恐近淮之民翻然改圖，青、冀二州猝未可拔也。」

translations.literal: In warfare speed is prized; if prolonged, change arises. If heaven's rain has already fallen, they may use the water to open passage, transport grain and increase their numbers, and plan advance— I fear the people near the Huai will suddenly change their plans, and the two provinces Qing and Ji cannot quickly be taken."
translations.idiomatic: War favors speed; delay breeds trouble. Once the rains come they may use the waterways, bring up grain and reinforcements, and strike back—I fear the Huai-border people will turn on us, and Qing and Ji will not fall quickly."

sentences.zh: 五月，壬戌，以太子詹事袁粲為尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on renxu, Yuan Can, Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, was made Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on renxu, Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent Yuan Can was appointed Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之自送運米至下邳，魏人遣清、泗間人詐攸之云：「薛安都欲降，求軍迎接。」

translations.literal: Shen Youzhi personally escorted transport grain to Xiapi. The people of Wei sent men from between the Qing and Si to deceive Youzhi, saying, "Xue Andu wishes to surrender and asks for an army to receive him."
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi personally convoyed grain to Xiapi. Wei agents from the Qing-Si region told him falsely that Xue Andu wished to surrender and begged for troops to escort him."

sentences.zh: 軍副吳喜請遣千人赴之，攸之不許。

translations.literal: The army deputy Wu Xi asked to send a thousand men to go; Youzhi did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy commander Wu Xi asked to send a thousand men; Youzhi refused.

sentences.zh: 既而來者益多，喜固請不已，攸之乃集來者告之曰：「君諸人既有誠心，若能與薛徐州子弟俱來者，皆即假君以本鄉縣，唯意所欲；

translations.literal: Afterward the comers grew more numerous; Xi pressed his request without cease. Youzhi then gathered the comers and told them, "You gentlemen already have sincere hearts; if you can come together with the sons and younger brothers of Xue of Xuzhou, all will immediately be granted your native commandery and county as you wish;
translations.idiomatic: More messengers kept coming and Xi pressed hard. Youzhi assembled them and said, "If you are sincere, bring the sons and brothers of Xue of Xuzhou with you and I will grant each of you his home district as you desire;

sentences.zh: 如其不爾，無為空勞往還。」

translations.literal: if it is not so, do not toil in vain going back and forth."
translations.idiomatic: otherwise do not waste your time running back and forth."

sentences.zh: 自是一去不返。

translations.literal: From then on none returned.
translations.idiomatic: After that not one came back.

sentences.zh: 攸之使軍主彭城陳顯達將千人助戍下邳而還。

translations.literal: Youzhi had the army commander Chen Xianda of Pengcheng lead a thousand men to help garrison Xiapi and then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi left army commander Chen Xianda of Pengcheng with a thousand men to reinforce Xiapi and marched back.

sentences.zh: 薛安都子伯令亡命梁、雍之間，聚黨數千人，攻陷郡縣。

translations.literal: Xue Andu's son Boling, an outlaw between Liang and Yong, gathered a party of several thousand men and attacked and took commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Andu's son Boling fled into the Liang and Yong region, raised several thousand followers, and overran districts and counties.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，雍州刺史巴陵王休若遣南陽太守張敬兒等擊斬之。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, the regional inspector of Yongzhou, the Prince of Baling Xiuruo, sent the Administrator of Nanyang Zhang Jinger and others to attack and behead him.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Yongzhou inspector Prince of Baling Xiuruo sent Nanyang administrator Zhang Jinger and others to attack and kill him.

sentences.zh: 上復遣中領軍沈攸之等擊彭城。

translations.literal: The emperor again sent the Central Army Commander Shen Youzhi and others to attack Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again dispatched Central Army Commander Shen Youzhi and others against Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 攸之以為清、泗方涸，糧運不繼，固執以為不可。

translations.literal: Youzhi thought the Qing and Si were just drying up and grain transport could not continue; he stubbornly held that it was impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi argued that the Qing and Si were drying up, grain could not be supplied, and the campaign was impossible.

sentences.zh: 使者七返，上怒，強遣之。

translations.literal: Envoys returned seven times; the emperor was angry and forced him to go.
translations.idiomatic: His envoys came back seven times; the emperor grew furious and ordered him out by force.

sentences.zh: 八月，壬寅，以攸之行南兗州刺史，將兵北出；

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on renyin, Youzhi was made acting regional inspector of Southern Yanzhou and led troops north;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on renyin, Youzhi was appointed acting inspector of Southern Yanzhou and marched north;

sentences.zh: 使行徐州事蕭道成將千人鎮淮陰。

translations.literal: Xiao Daocheng, acting for Xuzhou affairs, was sent with a thousand men to garrison Huaiyin.
translations.idiomatic: and Xiao Daocheng, acting administrator of Xuzhou, was sent with a thousand men to hold Huaiyin.

sentences.zh: 道成收養豪俊，賓客始盛。

translations.literal: Daocheng gathered and supported bold and talented men; his clients and guests began to flourish.
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng began gathering bold and able men, and his following of clients grew.

sentences.zh: 魏之入彭城也，垣崇祖將部曲奔朐山，據之，遣使來降；

translations.literal: When Wei entered Pengcheng, Yuan Chongzu led his personal forces and fled to Qushan, occupied it, and sent envoys to come and surrender;
translations.idiomatic: When Wei took Pengcheng, Yuan Chongzu led his household troops to Qushan, seized it, and sent envoys to submit;

sentences.zh: 蕭道成以為朐山戍主。

translations.literal: Xiao Daocheng made him garrison commander of Qushan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Daocheng appointed him commandant of Qushan.

sentences.zh: 朐山濱海孤絕，人情未安，崇祖浮舟水側，欲有急則逃入海。

translations.literal: Qushan bordered the sea, isolated and alone; hearts were not yet settled. Chongzu kept boats afloat on the water's edge, wishing that if there were urgency he could flee into the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Qushan stood alone on the coast and the people were uneasy; Chongzu kept boats moored offshore so that in an emergency he could escape by sea.

sentences.zh: 魏東徐州刺史成固公戍固城，崇祖部將有罪，亡降魏。

translations.literal: Cheng the Duke of Gu, regional inspector of Eastern Xuzhou of Wei, garrisoned Gucheng. A subordinate officer of Chongzu was guilty and fled in surrender to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's Eastern Xuzhou inspector Duke Cheng held Gucheng. One of Chongzu's officers who had committed a crime defected to Wei.

sentences.zh: 成固公遣步騎二萬襲朐山，去城二十里；

translations.literal: Cheng the Duke of Gu sent twenty thousand foot and horse to raid Qushan, twenty li from the city;
translations.idiomatic: Duke Cheng sent twenty thousand infantry and cavalry against Qushan, halting twenty li from the walls;

sentences.zh: 崇祖方出送客，城中人驚懼，皆下船欲去。

translations.literal: Chongzu was just out seeing off a guest; the people in the city were alarmed and afraid, and all went down to the boats wishing to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzu was seeing a guest off when panic spread through the city and everyone rushed for the boats.

sentences.zh: 崇祖還，謂腹心曰：「虜非有宿謀，承叛者之言而來耳，易誑也。

translations.literal: Chongzu returned and said to his trusted men, "The barbarians have no long-laid plan; they come on the word of the defector—that is easy to deceive.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzu came back and told his confidants, "The enemy have no real plan—they came on the defector's word and can be fooled.

sentences.zh: 今得百餘人還，事必濟矣。

translations.literal: Now if we get a hundred-odd men back, the affair will surely succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Bring back a hundred men and we can still win.

sentences.zh: 但人情一駭，不可斂集，卿等可亟去此一里外，大呼而來云：『艾塘義人已得破虜，須戍軍速往，相助逐之。』」

translations.literal: But once hearts are startled they cannot be gathered; you gentlemen can quickly go a li or so beyond here, shout loudly as you come, and say, 'The righteous men of Aitang have already broken the barbarians; the garrison troops must hurry to help drive them off.'
translations.idiomatic: But panic cannot be rallied at once—go a li beyond the walls, come back shouting that the men of Aitang have already routed the barbarians and the garrison must hurry to help pursue them.'

sentences.zh: 舟中人果喜，爭上岸。

translations.literal: The men in the boats were indeed pleased and scrambled ashore.
translations.idiomatic: The men on the boats rejoiced and scrambled ashore.

sentences.zh: 崇祖引入，據城；

translations.literal: Chongzu led them in and held the city;
translations.idiomatic: Chongzu brought them inside and held the walls;

sentences.zh: 遣羸弱入島，人持兩炬火，登山鼓噪。

translations.literal: he sent the weak into the islet, each man holding two torches, climbing the mountain and beating drums and shouting.
translations.idiomatic: sent the weaker men to an islet, each with two torches, to climb the heights and beat drums and shout.

sentences.zh: 魏參騎以為軍備甚盛，乃退。

translations.literal: The Wei scouting horsemen thought military preparations were very strong and therefore withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei scouts thought a great host was at hand and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 上以崇祖為北琅邪、蘭陵二郡太守。

translations.literal: The emperor made Chongzu administrator of the two commanderies Northern Langye and Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Chongzu administrator of Northern Langye and Lanling.

sentences.zh: 垣榮祖亦自彭城奔朐山，以奉使不效，畏罪不敢出，往依蕭道成於淮陰。

translations.literal: Yuan Rongzu also fled from Pengcheng to Qushan; because his mission as envoy had not succeeded, he feared punishment and did not dare go out, and went to rely on Xiao Daocheng at Huaiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Rongzu also fled from Pengcheng to Qushan; his mission had failed and fearing punishment he did not dare show himself, and went to join Xiao Daocheng at Huaiyin.

sentences.zh: 榮祖少學騎射，或謂之曰：「武事可畏，何不學書！」

translations.literal: Rongzu in youth studied riding and archery; someone said to him, "Military affairs are to be feared—why not study books!"
translations.idiomatic: Rongzu had trained in riding and archery from youth; someone said to him, "War is a grim trade—why not study the classics!"

sentences.zh: 榮祖曰：「昔曹公父子上馬橫槊，下馬談詠，此於天下，可不負飲食矣。

translations.literal: Rongzu said, "In old times Lord Cao and his sons mounted horse with spear across saddle, dismounted horse to converse and chant—by this they did not fail the world in food and drink.
translations.idiomatic: Rongzu replied, "Cao Cao and his sons could mount with spear in hand and dismount to recite poetry—that was enough to earn their bread under heaven.

sentences.zh: 君輩無自全之伎，何異犬羊乎！」

translations.literal: You gentlemen have no skill to preserve yourselves—how are you different from dogs and sheep!"
translations.idiomatic: You have no skill to save yourselves—you might as well be sheep!"

sentences.zh: 劉善明從弟僧副將部曲二千人，避魏居海島，道成亦召而撫之。

translations.literal: Liu Shanming's younger cousin Sengfu led two thousand men of his personal forces, avoided Wei and dwelt on a sea islet; Daocheng also summoned and comforted them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shanming's cousin Sengfu led two thousand household troops, took refuge from Wei on a coastal islet, and Daocheng summoned and comforted him as well.

sentences.zh: 魏於天宮寺作大像，高四十三尺，用銅十萬斤，黃金六百斤。

translations.literal: Wei made a great image at the Temple of the Heavenly Palace, forty-three chi high, using one hundred thousand jin of copper and six hundred jin of gold.
translations.idiomatic: Wei cast a great Buddha at the Temple of the Heavenly Palace, forty-three chi tall, using one hundred thousand jin of copper and six hundred jin of gold.

sentences.zh: 魏尉元遣孔伯恭帥步騎一萬拒沈攸之，又以攸之前敗所喪士卒瘃墮膝行者悉還攸之，以沮其氣。

translations.literal: Wei Yuan of Wei sent Kong Bogong to command ten thousand foot and horse to resist Shen Youzhi, and also returned to Youzhi all the soldiers lost in his former defeat who had suffered frostbite and lost toes and knees when walking— to dampen his spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's Wei Yuan sent Kong Bogong with ten thousand foot and horse to block Shen Youzhi, and returned to him every soldier crippled by frostbite from his earlier defeat—to break his morale.

sentences.zh: 上尋悔遣攸之等，復召使還。

translations.literal: The emperor soon regretted sending Youzhi and the others, and again summoned them to return.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor soon regretted dispatching Youzhi and recalled him.

sentences.zh: 攸之至焦墟，去下邳五十餘里，陳顯達引兵迎攸之至睢清口，伯恭擊破之。

translations.literal: Youzhi reached Jiaoxu, more than fifty li from Xiapi; Chen Xianda led troops to welcome Youzhi to Suiqingkou, and Bogong attacked and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi reached Jiaoxu, fifty-odd li from Xiapi; Chen Xianda marched to meet him at Suiqingkou, and Bogong routed them.

sentences.zh: 攸之引兵退，伯恭追擊之，攸之大敗，龍驤將軍姜彥之等戰沒。

translations.literal: Youzhi led the army in retreat; Bogong pursued and attacked; Youzhi was utterly defeated, and the Dragon Cavalry General Jiang Yanzhi and others died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi withdrew; Bogong pursued and crushed him. Dragon Cavalry General Jiang Yanzhi and others were killed.

sentences.zh: 攸之創重，入保顯達營；

translations.literal: Youzhi's wounds were grave; he entered to hold Xianda's camp;
translations.idiomatic: Badly wounded, Youzhi took refuge in Xianda's camp;

sentences.zh: 丁酉夜，眾潰，攸之輕騎南走，委棄軍資器械以萬計，還屯淮陰。

translations.literal: on the night of dingyou the masses collapsed; Youzhi fled south with light cavalry, abandoning military stores and weapons numbering in the tens of thousands, and returned to garrison Huaiyin.
translations.idiomatic: that night on dingyou the army broke; Youzhi fled south with a light escort, leaving tens of thousands of weapons and supplies behind, and withdrew to Huaiyin.

sentences.zh: 尉元以書諭徐州刺史王玄載，玄載棄下邳走，魏以隴西辛紹先為下邳太守。

translations.literal: Wei Yuan with a letter instructed Wang Xuanzai, regional inspector of Xuzhou; Xuanzai abandoned Xiapi and fled. Wei made Xin Shaoxian of Longxi administrator of Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yuan wrote to Xuzhou inspector Wang Xuanzai, who abandoned Xiapi and fled. Wei appointed Xin Shaoxian of Longxi as administrator of Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 紹先不尚苛察，務舉大綱，教民治生禦寇而已；

translations.literal: Shaoxian did not esteem harsh scrutiny; he devoted himself to setting forth the great outline, teaching the people to manage livelihood and resist bandits—that was all;
translations.idiomatic: Shaoxian was no stickler for petty rules; he laid down broad principles, taught the people to make a living and guard against raiders, and nothing more;

sentences.zh: 由是下邳安之。

translations.literal: because of this Xiapi was at peace.
translations.idiomatic: and so Xiapi was pacified.

sentences.zh: 孔伯恭進攻宿豫，宿豫戍將魯僧遵亦棄城走。

translations.literal: Kong Bogong advanced to attack Suqian; the Suqian garrison commander Lu Sengzun also abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Bogong attacked Suqian, and its garrison commander Lu Sengzun fled as well.

sentences.zh: 魏將孔大恆等將千騎南攻淮陽，淮陽太守崔武仲焚城走。

translations.literal: The Wei generals Kong Daheng and others led a thousand horsemen south to attack Huaiyang; Cui Wuzhong, administrator of Huaiyang, burned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Wei generals Kong Daheng and others led a thousand horse south against Huaiyang; administrator Cui Wuzhong burned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 慕容白曜進屯瑕丘。

translations.literal: Murong Baiyao advanced and encamped at Xiaqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Baiyao advanced and camped at Xiaqiu.

sentences.zh: 崔道固之未降也，綏邊將軍房法壽為王玄邈司馬，屢破道固軍，歷城人畏之。

translations.literal: Before Cui Daogu had surrendered, the General Who Pacifies the Borders Fang Fashou was Wang Xuanmiao's Major and repeatedly defeated Daogu's army; the people of Licheng feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Before Cui Daogu submitted, Border-Pacifying General Fang Fashou, as Wang Xuanmiao's major, had repeatedly beaten Daogu's forces, and the people of Licheng stood in awe of him.

sentences.zh: 及道固降，皆罷兵。

translations.literal: When Daogu surrendered, all disbanded their troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Daogu surrendered, the militias were disbanded.

sentences.zh: 道固畏法壽扇動百姓，迫遣法壽使還建康。

translations.literal: Daogu feared that Fashou would stir up the common people and compelled Fashou to go as envoy back to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Daogu feared Fashou would rouse the populace and forced him to go to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 會從弟崇吉自升城來，以母妻為魏所獲，謀於法壽。

translations.literal: It happened that his younger cousin Chongji came from Shengcheng; because mother and wife had been captured by Wei, he plotted with Fashou.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Chongji arrived from Shengcheng; his mother and wife had been taken by Wei, and he plotted with Fashou.

sentences.zh: 法壽雅不欲南行，怨道固迫之。

translations.literal: Fashou by nature did not wish to go south and resented Daogu for forcing him.
translations.idiomatic: Fashou had never wanted to go south and resented Daogu for pushing him.

sentences.zh: 時道固遣兼治中房靈賓督清河、廣川二郡事，戍磐陽，法壽乃與崇吉謀襲磐陽，據之，降於慕容白曜，以贖崇吉母妻。

translations.literal: At this time Daogu sent the concurrent Supervisor of the Masters Fang Lingbin to oversee the affairs of the two commanderies Qinghe and Guangchuan and garrison Panyang. Fashou then with Chongji plotted to surprise Panyang, seize it, and surrender to Murong Baiyao to ransom Chongji's mother and wife.
translations.idiomatic: Daogu had sent concurrent Supervisor Fang Lingbin to oversee Qinghe and Guangchuan and garrison Panyang. Fashou and Chongji seized Panyang by surprise, held it, and surrendered to Murong Baiyao to ransom Chongji's family.

sentences.zh: 道固遣兵攻之，白曜自瑕丘遣將軍長孫觀救磐陽，道固兵退。

translations.literal: Daogu sent troops to attack them; Baiyao from Xiaqiu sent the general Changsun Guan to rescue Panyang, and Daogu's troops withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Daogu sent troops against them; Baiyao dispatched General Changsun Guan from Xiaqiu to relieve Panyang, and Daogu's men withdrew.

sentences.zh: 白曜表冠軍將軍韓麒麟與法壽對為冀州刺史，以法壽從弟靈民、思順、靈悅、伯憐、伯玉、叔玉、思安、幼安等八人皆為郡守。

translations.literal: Baiyao memorialized that the General Who Conquers Champions Han Qilin and Fashou should be made regional inspectors of Jizhou in counterpart, and that Fashou's eight younger cousins Lingmin, Sishun, Lingyue, Bolian, Boyu, Shuyu, Si'an, and You'an should all be made commandery administrators.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao recommended that General Who Conquers Champions Han Qilin and Fashou serve jointly as inspectors of Jizhou, and appointed eight of Fashou's cousins—Lingmin, Sishun, Lingyue, Bolian, Boyu, Shuyu, Si'an, and You'an—as commandery administrators.

sentences.zh: 白曜自瑕丘引兵攻崔道固於歷城，遣平東將軍長孫陵等攻沈文秀於東陽。

translations.literal: Baiyao from Xiaqiu led troops to attack Cui Daogu at Licheng, and sent the General Who Pacifies the East Changsun Ling and others to attack Shen Wenxiu at Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao marched from Xiaqiu against Cui Daogu at Licheng and sent General Who Pacifies the East Changsun Ling and others against Shen Wenxiu at Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 道固拒守不降，白曜築長圍守之。

translations.literal: Daogu resisted and held without surrendering; Baiyao built a long encirclement to besiege him.
translations.idiomatic: Daogu held out; Baiyao invested the city with a long siege.

sentences.zh: 陵等至東陽，文秀請降；

translations.literal: Ling and the others reached Dongyang; Wenxiu requested surrender;
translations.idiomatic: Ling reached Dongyang and Wenxiu offered to surrender;

sentences.zh: 陵等入其西郭，縱士卒暴掠。

translations.literal: Ling and the others entered his western outer ward and let the soldiers rampage and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Ling entered the western suburb and let his men loot at will.

sentences.zh: 文秀悔怒，閉城拒守，擊陵等，破之。

translations.literal: Wenxiu, regretful and angry, closed the city and resisted, attacked Ling and the others, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu, furious at the looting, shut the gates, fought back, and routed Ling.

sentences.zh: 陵等退屯清西，屢進攻城，不克。

translations.literal: Ling and the others withdrew to camp west of Qing, repeatedly advanced to attack the city, and could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Ling withdrew west of Qing and assaulted the city again and again without success.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，大赦。

translations.literal: On guimao, a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 戊申，魏主李夫人生子宏。

translations.literal: On wushen, the Wei ruler's Lady Li gave birth to a son, Hong.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen Lady Li, consort of the Wei emperor, bore a son named Hong.

sentences.zh: 夫人，惠之女也。

translations.literal: The lady was the daughter of Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li was a daughter of Li Hui.

sentences.zh: 馮太后自撫養宏；

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Feng herself nurtured Hong;
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Feng raised the child herself;

sentences.zh: 頃之，還政於魏主。

translations.literal: before long she returned government to the Wei ruler.
translations.idiomatic: and soon restored rule to the Wei emperor.

sentences.zh: 魏主始親國事，勤於為治，賞罰嚴明，拔清節，黜貪污，於是魏之牧守始有以廉潔著聞者。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler then personally attended to state affairs, was diligent in governance, rewards and punishments were strict and clear, the upright and incorruptible were promoted and the greedy dismissed—thereupon among Wei's regional inspectors and administrators there began to be those famed for integrity and purity.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor now took up state affairs in person, governed diligently, rewarded and punished without favor, promoted the upright and removed the corrupt—and for the first time Wei's provincial officials became known for integrity.

sentences.zh: 太中大夫徐爰，自太祖時用事，素不禮於上。

translations.literal: The Grandee of Splendid Happiness Xu Ai, since the time of the founding emperor had held power and by nature had not been courteous to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Grandee of Splendid Happiness Xu Ai had held power since the founding emperor's day and had never shown the present emperor proper respect.

sentences.zh: 上銜之，詔數其奸佞之罪，徙交州。

translations.literal: The emperor bore a grudge against him, issued an edict enumerating his crimes of treachery and flattery, and banished him to Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor resented him, issued an edict listing his crimes of treachery and flattery, and exiled him to Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，辛巳，詔徙義陽王昶為晉熙王，使員外郎李豐以金千兩贖昶於魏。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on xinsi, an edict moved Prince of Yiyang Chang to be Prince of Jinxi, and sent the Staff Officer Li Feng with a thousand liang of gold to ransom Chang from Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on xinsi an edict transferred Prince of Yiyang Chang to the title Prince of Jinxi and sent staff officer Li Feng with a thousand liang of gold to ransom him from Wei.

sentences.zh: 魏人弗許，使昶與上書，為兄弟之儀。

translations.literal: The people of Wei did not permit it and had Chang write to the emperor with the etiquette of brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Wei refused and had Chang write to the Song emperor as a brother would.

sentences.zh: 上責其不稱臣，不答。

translations.literal: The emperor blamed him for not calling himself a subject and did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked him for not addressing him as sovereign and sent no answer.

sentences.zh: 魏主復使昶與上書，昶辭曰：「臣本實彧兄，未經為臣。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler again had Chang write to the emperor; Chang declined, saying, "Your servant was in truth the elder brother of Yu and has never been a subject.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor had Chang write again; Chang refused, saying, "I was in truth Emperor Yu's elder brother and was never his subject.

sentences.zh: 若改前書，事為二敬；

translations.literal: If I change the former letter, the affair becomes two forms of respect;
translations.idiomatic: To change my earlier letter would be to offer two kinds of deference;

sentences.zh: 敬或不改，彼所不納。

translations.literal: if respect is changed or not changed, that side will not accept.
translations.idiomatic: whether I change it or not, he will not accept it.

sentences.zh: 臣不敢奉詔。」

translations.literal: Your servant does not dare obey the edict."
translations.idiomatic: I dare not obey this command."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: Thereupon it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 魏人愛重昶，凡三尚公主。

translations.literal: The people of Wei loved and esteemed Chang; in all he married three imperial princesses.
translations.idiomatic: Wei held Chang in high regard; he married three imperial princesses in succession.

sentences.zh: 十一月，乙卯，分徐州置東徐州，以輔國將軍張讜為刺史。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on yimao, Xuzhou was divided to establish Eastern Xuzhou, and the General Who Assists the State Zhang Dan was made regional inspector.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on yimao, Eastern Xuzhou was carved out of Xuzhou and General Who Assists the State Zhang Dan was made its inspector.

sentences.zh: 十二月，庚戌，以幽州刺史劉休賓為兗州刺史。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on gengxu, Liu Xiubin, regional inspector of Youzhou, was made regional inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on gengxu Youzhou inspector Liu Xiubin was appointed inspector of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 休賓之妻，崔邪利之女也，生子文曄，與邪利皆沒於魏。

translations.literal: Xiubin's wife was the daughter of Cui Xieli; she bore a son Wenyue, and with Xieli both were lost to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Xiubin's wife was Cui Xieli's daughter; she bore a son named Wenyue, and she and Xieli were both taken by Wei.

sentences.zh: 慕容白曜將其妻子至梁鄒城下示之。

translations.literal: Murong Baiyao brought his wife and son to beneath the walls of Liangzou and displayed them.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Baiyao brought them beneath the walls of Liangzou and displayed them to Xiubin.

sentences.zh: 休賓密遣主簿尹文達至歷城見白曜，且視其妻子；

translations.literal: Xiubin secretly sent his Registrar Yin Wenda to Licheng to see Baiyao and also to view his wife and son;
translations.idiomatic: Xiubin secretly sent his registrar Yin Wenda to Licheng to see Baiyao and look upon his family;

sentences.zh: 休賓欲降，而兄子聞慰不可。

translations.literal: Xiubin wished to surrender, but his elder brother's son Wen Wei would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Xiubin wished to surrender, but his nephew Wen Wei forbade it.

sentences.zh: 白曜使人至城下呼曰：「劉休賓數遣人來見僕射約降，何故違期不至！」

translations.literal: Baiyao sent a man to beneath the walls to shout, "Liu Xiubin has repeatedly sent men to see the Vice Director and arrange surrender—why do you break the appointed time and not come!"
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao had a man call from below the walls, "Liu Xiubin has sent envoys again and again to arrange surrender with the Vice Director—why do you fail to keep your word!"

sentences.zh: 由是城中皆知之，共禁制休賓不得降，魏兵圍之。

translations.literal: Thereupon everyone in the city knew of it; together they restrained Xiubin from surrendering, and Wei troops besieged the city.
translations.idiomatic: The whole city heard; together they prevented Xiubin from surrendering, and Wei troops invested the city.

sentences.zh: 魏西河公石復攻汝陰，汝陰有備，無功而還。

translations.literal: Wei's Duke of Xihe, Shi, again attacked Ruyin; Ruyin was prepared and he returned without achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's Duke of Xihe, Shi, attacked Ruyin again, but the city was ready and he withdrew without success.

sentences.zh: 常珍奇雖降於魏，實懷貳心；

translations.literal: Chang Zhenqi although he had surrendered to Wei, in truth harbored a divided heart;
translations.idiomatic: Although Chang Zhenqi had submitted to Wei, he still harbored divided loyalties;

sentences.zh: 劉勉復以書招之。

translations.literal: Liu Mian again with a letter summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mian again wrote to win him back.

sentences.zh: 會西河公石攻汝陰，珍奇乘虛燒劫懸瓠，驅掠上蔡、安成、平輿三縣民，屯於灌水。

translations.literal: It happened that the Duke of Xihe, Shi, attacked Ruyin; Zhenqi seized the opening to burn and plunder Xuanhu, drove and carried off the people of the three counties Shangcai, Ancheng, and Pingyu, and encamped at Guanshui.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke of Xihe Shi attacked Ruyin, Zhenqi seized the chance to raid Xuanhu, drove off the people of Shangcai, Ancheng, and Pingyu, and encamped at Guanshui.

sentences.zh: 太宗明皇帝中泰始四年（

translations.literal: Fourth year of Taishi of Emperor Ming of Northern Wei (
translations.idiomatic: Fourth year of the Taishi reign of Emperor Ming of Northern Wei (

sentences.zh: 戊申，公元四六八年）

translations.literal: wushen, CE 468)
translations.idiomatic: wushen, 468 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，己未，上祀南郊，大赦。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on jiwei, the emperor sacrificed at the southern suburb and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on jiwei the emperor sacrificed at the southern suburb and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 魏汝陽司馬趙懷仁帥眾寇武津，豫州刺史劉勉遣龍驤將軍申元德擊破之，又斬魏於都公閼於拔於汝陽台東，獲運車千三百乘。

translations.literal: Wei's Major of Ruyang Zhao Huairen commanded the masses to raid Wujin; Liu Mian, regional inspector of Yuzhou, sent the Dragon Cavalry General Shen Yuande to attack and defeat him, and also beheaded the Duke of Yudu, Yubaba, east of the Ruyang terrace, capturing thirteen hundred transport carts.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's Ruyang major Zhao Huairen raided Wujin; Yuzhou inspector Liu Mian sent Dragon Cavalry General Shen Yuande to rout him and beheaded Wei's Duke of Yudu, Yubaba, east of the Ruyang terrace, seizing thirteen hundred supply wagons.

sentences.zh: 魏復寇義陽，勉使司徒參軍孫台瓘擊破之。

translations.literal: Wei again raided Yiyang; Mian had the Staff Officer of the Minister of Education Sun Taiguan attack and defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: Wei raided Yiyang again; Mian's staff officer Sun Taiguan defeated them.

sentences.zh: 淮西民賈元友上書，陳伐魏取陳、蔡之策，上以其書示劉勉。

translations.literal: Jia Yuanyou, a commoner of Huai west, submitted a memorial setting forth a plan to attack Wei and take Chen and Cai; the emperor showed his memorial to Liu Mian.
translations.idiomatic: A Huai-western commoner named Jia Yuanyou memorialized with a plan to attack Wei and recover Chen and Cai; the emperor showed it to Liu Mian.

sentences.zh: 勉上言：「元友稱『虜主幼弱，內外多難，天亡有期』。

translations.literal: Mian submitted, saying, "Yuanyou states, 'The barbarian ruler is young and weak, within and without there are many difficulties, and heaven's destruction has its term.'
translations.idiomatic: Mian replied, "Yuanyou claims that 'the barbarian ruler is young and weak, troubles abound within and without, and their doom is near.'

sentences.zh: 臣以為虜自去冬蹈藉王土，磐據數郡，百姓殘亡；

translations.literal: Your servant thinks that since last winter the barbarians have trampled the royal soil and firmly held several commanderies; the common people are ruined and dead;
translations.idiomatic: I believe that since last winter the barbarians have trampled our soil, seized several commanderies, and slaughtered the people;

sentences.zh: 今春以來，連城圍逼，國家未能復境，何暇滅虜！

translations.literal: from this spring onward, linked cities are besieged and pressed; the state has not been able to recover its borders—what leisure to destroy the barbarians!
translations.idiomatic: this spring city after city has been besieged, and we have not even recovered our borders—how can we talk of destroying the barbarians!

sentences.zh: 元友所陳，率多夸誕狂謀，皆非實。

translations.literal: What Yuanyou set forth is mostly exaggerated, wild schemes, none of it real.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyou's proposals are mostly boastful fantasies, none of them true.

sentences.zh: 言之甚易，行之甚難。

translations.literal: To speak of it is very easy; to carry it out is very hard.
translations.idiomatic: Easy to say, hard to do.

sentences.zh: 臣竊尋元嘉以來，傖荒遠人，多干國議，負擔歸闕，皆勸討虜，從來信納，皆貽後悔。

translations.literal: Your servant privately recalls that since the Yuanjia era, distant men from the northern wilds have often interfered in state deliberations, shouldered burdens and returned to the court, all urging attack on the barbarians—every time such counsel was believed and adopted, regret followed.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Yuanjia era, men from the northern frontier have come to court laden with advice to attack the barbarians—and every time such counsel was heeded, we lived to regret it.

sentences.zh: 境上之人，唯視強弱：王師至彼，必壺漿候塗；

translations.literal: The people on the borders look only at strength and weakness: when the royal army reaches them, they are sure to bring pots of drink and wait by the road;
translations.idiomatic: Border people follow strength alone: when our armies arrive they greet us with wine along the road;

sentences.zh: 裁見退軍，便抄截蜂起。

translations.literal: barely see the army withdraw, and at once they raid and intercept like swarming bees.
translations.idiomatic: the moment our troops withdraw they swarm out to cut us off.

sentences.zh: 此前後所見，明驗非一也。」

translations.literal: What has been seen before and after is clear proof, not once alone."
translations.idiomatic: We have seen this proved again and again."

sentences.zh: 上乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dropped the plan.

sentences.zh: 魏尉元遣使說東徐州刺史張讜，讜以團城降魏。

translations.literal: Wei Yuan of Wei sent envoys to persuade Zhang Dan, regional inspector of Eastern Xuzhou; Dan with Tuancheng surrendered to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's Wei Yuan sent envoys to win over Eastern Xuzhou inspector Zhang Dan, who surrendered Tuancheng to Wei.

sentences.zh: 魏以中書侍郎高閭與讜對為東徐州刺史，李璨與畢眾敬對為東兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Wei made the Secretariat Gentleman Gao Lu counterpart regional inspector of Eastern Xuzhou with Dan, and Li Can counterpart regional inspector of Eastern Yanzhou with Bi Zhongjing.
translations.idiomatic: Wei paired Secretariat Gentleman Gao Lu with Dan as joint inspectors of Eastern Xuzhou, and Li Can with Bi Zhongjing as joint inspectors of Eastern Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 無又說兗州刺史王整、蘭陵太守桓忻，整、忻皆降於魏。

translations.literal: Yuan again persuaded Wang Zheng, regional inspector of Yanzhou, and Huan Xin, administrator of Lanling; Zheng and Xin both surrendered to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan also won over Yanzhou inspector Wang Zheng and Lanling administrator Huan Xin, and both submitted to Wei.

sentences.zh: 魏以元為開府儀同三司、都督徐、南、北兗三州諸軍事、徐州刺史，鎮彭城。

translations.literal: Wei made Yuan Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, Commander-in-Chief of the Military Affairs of the three provinces Xu, Southern Yan, and Northern Yan, regional inspector of Xuzhou, garrisoning Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wei appointed Yuan Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, commander of military affairs in Xu, Southern Yan, and Northern Yan, inspector of Xuzhou, with his seat at Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 召薛安都、畢眾敬入朝，至平城，魏以上客待之，群從皆封侯，賜第宅，資給甚厚。

translations.literal: Xue Andu and Bi Zhongjing were summoned to court; when they reached Pingcheng, Wei treated them as honored guests, all their followers were enfeoffed as marquises, mansions were granted, and provisions were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Andu and Bi Zhongjing were summoned to court; at Pingcheng Wei received them as honored guests, enfeoffed their followers as marquises, granted them mansions, and lavished gifts upon them.

sentences.zh: 慕容白曜圍歷城經年，二月，庚寅，拔其東郭；

translations.literal: Murong Baiyao besieged Licheng for a year; in the second month, on gengyin, he took its eastern outer ward;
translations.idiomatic: Murong Baiyao had besieged Licheng for a year; in the second month, on gengyin, he took the eastern suburb;

sentences.zh: 癸巳，崔道固面縛出降。

translations.literal: on guisi, Cui Daogu came out bound with face exposed and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: on guisi Cui Daogu came out with hands bound and face bare to surrender.

sentences.zh: 白曜遣道固之子景業與劉文曄同至梁鄒，劉休賓亦出降。

translations.literal: Baiyao sent Daogu's son Jingye together with Liu Wenyue to Liangzou, and Liu Xiubin also came out and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao sent Daogu's son Jingye and Liu Wenyue to Liangzou, and Liu Xiubin surrendered as well.

sentences.zh: 白曜送道固、休賓及其僚屬於平城。

translations.literal: Baiyao sent Daogu, Xiubin, and their subordinates to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao sent Daogu, Xiubin, and their staffs to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，以前龍驤將軍常珍奇為都督司、北豫二州諸軍事、司州刺史。

translations.literal: On xinchou, the former Dragon Cavalry General Chang Zhenqi was made Commander-in-Chief of the Military Affairs of the two provinces Si and Northern Yu, regional inspector of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou former Dragon Cavalry General Chang Zhenqi was appointed commander of military affairs in Si and Northern Yu and inspector of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 魏西河公石攻之，珍奇單騎奔壽陽。

translations.literal: Wei's Duke of Xihe, Shi, attacked him; Zhenqi fled on a single horse to Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's Duke of Xihe, Shi, attacked him, and Zhenqi fled alone to Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，車騎大將軍、曲江莊公王玄謨卒。

translations.literal: On yisi, the General of Chariots and Cavalry, the Duke of Qujiang Zhuang, Wang Xuanmo, died.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi General of Chariots and Cavalry, Duke of Qujiang Zhuang Wang Xuanmo, died.

sentences.zh: 三月，魏慕容白曜進圍東陽。

translations.literal: In the third month, Murong Baiyao of Wei advanced to besiege Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Murong Baiyao of Wei advanced to besiege Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 上以崔道固兄子僧祐為輔國將軍，將兵數千從海道救歷城，至不其，聞歷城已沒，遂降於魏。

translations.literal: The emperor made Cui Daogu's elder brother's son Sengyou General Who Assists the State, to lead several thousand troops by sea to rescue Licheng; when he reached Buqi he heard Licheng had fallen and thereupon surrendered to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Daogu's nephew Sengyou General Who Assists the State and sent him with several thousand men by sea to relieve Licheng; at Buqi he learned the city had fallen and surrendered to Wei.

sentences.zh: 交州刺史劉牧卒。

translations.literal: Liu Mu, regional inspector of Jiaozhou, died.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaozhou inspector Liu Mu died.

sentences.zh: 州人李長仁殺牧北來部曲，據州反，自稱刺史。

translations.literal: Li Changren of the province killed Mu's northern followers and personal forces, seized the province and rebelled, and styled himself regional inspector.
translations.idiomatic: A local man named Li Changren killed Mu's northern troops, seized the province, rebelled, and styled himself inspector.

sentences.zh: 廣州刺史羊希使晉康太守沛郡劉思道伐俚。

translations.literal: Yang Xi, regional inspector of Guangzhou, had Liu Sidao of Pei, administrator of Jinkang, attack the Li.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhou inspector Yang Xi sent Jinkang administrator Liu Sidao of Pei against the Li.

sentences.zh: 思道違節度，失利，希遣收之；

translations.literal: Sidao violated command discipline and suffered defeat; Xi sent to arrest him;
translations.idiomatic: Sidao disobeyed orders, was defeated, and Xi sent to arrest him;

sentences.zh: 思道自帥所領攻州，希兵敗而死。

translations.literal: Sidao himself led those he commanded to attack the province; Xi's troops were defeated and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Sidao turned his own troops against the province; Xi's force was beaten and he was killed.

sentences.zh: 龍驤將軍陳伯紹將兵伐俚，還，擊思道，擒斬之。

translations.literal: The Dragon Cavalry General Chen Bozhao led troops to attack the Li; on his return he struck Sidao, captured and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Dragon Cavalry General Chen Bozhao, returning from campaigning against the Li, attacked Sidao, captured him, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 希，玄保之兄子也。

translations.literal: Xi was the nephew of Xuanbao.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was a nephew of Yang Xuanbao.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，己卯，復減郡縣田租之半。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on jimao, the land tax of commanderies and counties was again reduced by half.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on jimao the land tax of commanderies and counties was again cut by half.

sentences.zh: 徙東海王禕為廬江王，山陽王休祐為晉平王。

translations.literal: Prince of Donghai Yi was moved to be Prince of Lujiang; Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou was made Prince of Jinping.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Donghai Yi was transferred to Prince of Lujiang; Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou was made Prince of Jinping.

sentences.zh: 上以廢帝謂禕為驢王，故以廬江封之。

translations.literal: The emperor because the deposed emperor had called Yi the Donkey Prince, therefore enfeoffed him with Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Because the deposed emperor had called Yi the Donkey Prince, the present emperor enfeoffed him with Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 劉勉敗魏兵於許昌。

translations.literal: Liu Mian defeated Wei troops at Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mian defeated Wei forces at Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 魏以南郡公李惠為征南大將軍、儀同三司、都督關右諸軍事、雍州刺史，進爵為王。

translations.literal: Wei made the Duke of Nanjun Li Hui General-in-Chief Who Conquers the South, Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, Commander-in-Chief of the Military Affairs west of the Passes, regional inspector of Yongzhou, and advanced his rank to king.
translations.idiomatic: Wei appointed Duke of Nanjun Li Hui General-in-Chief Who Conquers the South, Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, commander of military affairs west of the passes, inspector of Yongzhou, and raised him to king.

sentences.zh: 五月，乙卯，魏主畋於崞山，道如繁畤，辛酉，還宮。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on yimao, the Wei ruler hunted at Mount Guo, went by way of Fanzhi, and on xinyou returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on yimao the Wei emperor hunted at Mount Guo, traveled by way of Fanzhi, and on xinyou returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 六月，魏以昌黎王馮熙為太傅。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Wei made the Prince of Changli Feng Xi Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Wei appointed Prince of Changli Feng Xi Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 熙，太后之兄也。

translations.literal: Xi was the empress dowager's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was the empress dowager's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，庚申，以驍騎將軍蕭道成為南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on gengshen, the Valiant Cavalry General Xiao Daocheng was made regional inspector of Southern Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on gengshen Valiant Cavalry General Xiao Daocheng was appointed inspector of Southern Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 八月，戊子，以南康相劉勃為交州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on wuzi, Liu Bo, Chancellor of Nankang, was made regional inspector of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on wuzi Nankang chancellor Liu Bo was appointed inspector of Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 上以沈文秀之弟征北中兵參軍文靜為輔國將軍，統高密等五郡軍事，自海道救東陽。

translations.literal: The emperor made Shen Wenxiu's younger brother Wenjing, Central Army Major of the Army of the North, General Who Assists the State, commanding the military affairs of five commanderies including Gaomi, to rescue Dongyang by sea.
