translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Wenxiu's younger brother Wenjing, a major in the Army of the North, as General Who Assists the State to command five commanderies including Gaomi and sail to relieve Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 至不其城，為魏所斷，因保城自固。

translations.literal: When he reached Bucheng he was cut off by Wei and therefore held the city and strengthened himself.
translations.idiomatic: At Bucheng he was cut off by Wei and held the city to defend himself.

sentences.zh: 魏人攻之，不克。

translations.literal: The people of Wei attacked it but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Wei attacked but could not take it.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，分青州置東青州，以文靜為刺史。

translations.literal: On xinmao, Qingzhou was divided to establish Eastern Qingzhou, and Wenjing was made regional inspector.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao Eastern Qingzhou was carved out of Qingzhou and Wenjing was made its inspector.

sentences.zh: 九月，辛亥，魏立皇叔楨為南安王，長壽為城陽王，太洛為章武王，休為安定王。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on xinhai, Wei established the emperor's uncle Zhen as Prince of Nan'an, Changshou as Prince of Chengyang, Tailuo as Prince of Zhangwu, and Xiu as Prince of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on xinhai Wei enfeoffed the emperor's uncle Zhen as Prince of Nan'an, Changshou as Prince of Chengyang, Tailuo as Prince of Zhangwu, and Xiu as Prince of Anding.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，癸酉朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the first day guiyou, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on the new moon of guiyou, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 發諸州兵北伐。

translations.literal: Troops of the various provinces were mobilized for a northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Troops from the provinces were mobilized for a northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 十一月，李長仁遣使請降，自貶行州事；

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Li Changren sent envoys to request surrender and demoted himself to acting for provincial affairs;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Li Changren sent envoys to offer surrender and demoted himself to acting inspector;

sentences.zh: 許之。

translations.literal: this was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: the court accepted.

sentences.zh: 十二月，魏人拔不其城，殺沈文靜，入東陽西郭。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the people of Wei took Bucheng, killed Shen Wenjing, and entered the western outer ward of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Wei took Bucheng, killed Shen Wenjing, and entered the western suburb of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 義嘉之亂，巫師請發修寧陵，戮玄宮為厭勝。

translations.literal: In the turmoil of Yijia, shamans requested opening the Xiuning tomb and destroying the inner palace as a charm to overcome evil.
translations.idiomatic: During the turmoil of Yijia, shamans asked to open the Xiuning tomb and desecrate the inner chamber as a charm against evil.

sentences.zh: 是歲，改葬昭太后。

translations.literal: In this year the Empress Dowager Zhao was reburied.
translations.idiomatic: That year Empress Dowager Zhao was reburied.

sentences.zh: 先是，中書侍郎、舍人皆以名流為之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Secretariat Gentlemen and Masters of Writing Attendants were all men of famous reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, Secretariat Gentlemen and Masters of Writing Attendants had been drawn from eminent families.

sentences.zh: 太祖始用寒士秋當，世祖猶雜選士庶，巢尚之、戴法興皆用事。

translations.literal: The founding emperor first employed the humble scholar Qiu Dang; the succeeding emperor still mixed selection of gentry and commoners—Chao Shangzhi and Dai Faxing both held power.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor first employed the humble scholar Qiu Dang; the succeeding emperor still mixed gentry and commoners in office—Chao Shangzhi and Dai Faxing both wielded power.

sentences.zh: 及上即位，盡用左右細人，游擊將軍阮佃夫、中書通事舍人王道隆、員外散騎侍郎楊運長等，並參預政事，權亞人主，巢、戴所不及也。

translations.literal: When the present emperor ascended, he employed entirely petty men at his side—the Mobile General Ruan Tianfu, the Secretariat Attendant for Current Affairs Wang Daolong, the Staff Gentleman of the Outer Retinue Yang Yunchang, and others—all participating in government, their power second only to the ruler, beyond what Chao and Dai could reach.
translations.idiomatic: When the present emperor took the throne he relied entirely on petty favorites at his side—Mobile General Ruan Tianfu, Secretariat Attendant for Current Affairs Wang Daolong, staff gentleman Yang Yunchang, and others—all sharing in government with power second only to the throne, far beyond what Chao and Dai had enjoyed.

sentences.zh: 佃夫尤恣橫，人有順迕，禍福立至。

translations.literal: Tianfu was especially overbearing and violent; whether a man complied or opposed, fortune or disaster came at once.
translations.idiomatic: Tianfu was the most overbearing of all; comply with him and prosper, cross him and perish at once.

sentences.zh: 大納貨賂，所餉減二百匹絹，則不報書。

translations.literal: He greatly received bribes; if what was offered was two hundred bolts of silk short, he would not reply with a letter.
translations.idiomatic: He took bribes on a vast scale; gifts short by two hundred bolts of silk earned no acknowledgment.

sentences.zh: 園宅飲饌，過於諸王；

translations.literal: His gardens, mansions, drink, and food surpassed the princes;
translations.idiomatic: His estates, feasts, and luxuries surpassed those of the princes;

sentences.zh: 妓樂服飾，宮掖不如也。

translations.literal: his courtesans, music, and dress—the inner palace was not his equal.
translations.idiomatic: his courtesans, music, and dress outshone even the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 朝士貴賤，莫不自結。

translations.literal: Court officials high and low, none failed to attach themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials high and low all sought his favor.

sentences.zh: 僕隸皆不次除官，捉車人至虎賁中郎部，馬士至員外郎。

translations.literal: Servants were all promoted out of turn; cart-holders reached the Tiger Guard Central Commandant's section, grooms reached Staff Officer.
translations.idiomatic: His servants were promoted out of turn—cart drivers to the Tiger Guard, grooms to staff officer.

sentences.zh: 太宗明皇帝中泰始五年（

translations.literal: Fifth year of Taishi of Emperor Ming of Northern Wei (
translations.idiomatic: Fifth year of the Taishi reign of Emperor Ming of Northern Wei (

sentences.zh: 己酉，公元四六九年）

translations.literal: jiyou, CE 469)
translations.idiomatic: jiyou, 469 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，癸亥，上耕籍田，大赦。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on guihai, the emperor plowed the sacred field and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on guihai the emperor plowed the sacred field and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 沈文秀守東陽，魏人圍之三年，外無救援，士卒晝夜拒戰，甲冑生蟣虱，無離叛之志。

translations.literal: Shen Wenxiu held Dongyang; the people of Wei besieged it three years; outside there was no rescue; soldiers day and night resisted in battle; armor and helmets bred lice; there was no mind to desert.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Wenxiu held Dongyang while Wei besieged it for three years without relief; his men fought day and night until lice bred in their armor, yet none deserted.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，魏人拔東陽，文秀解戎服，正衣冠，取所持節坐齋內。

translations.literal: On yichou the people of Wei took Dongyang; Wenxiu removed his military dress, straightened cap and robes, took the staff of office he held, and sat within the study.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou Wei took Dongyang; Wenxiu laid aside his armor, straightened his robes, took his staff of office, and sat in his study.

sentences.zh: 魏兵交至，問：「沈文秀何在？」

translations.literal: Wei soldiers arrived in a crowd and asked, "Where is Shen Wenxiu?"
translations.idiomatic: Wei soldiers crowded in and asked, "Where is Shen Wenxiu?"

sentences.zh: 文秀厲聲曰：「身是！」

translations.literal: Wenxiu in a stern voice said, "This person is he!"
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu answered in a stern voice, "I am he!"

sentences.zh: 魏人執之，去其衣，縛送慕容白曜，使之拜，文秀曰：「各兩國大臣，何拜之有！」

translations.literal: The people of Wei seized him, removed his clothes, bound him and sent him to Murong Baiyao, and made him bow. Wenxiu said, "Each is a great minister of two states—what bowing is there!"
translations.idiomatic: They seized him, stripped him, bound him, and sent him to Murong Baiyao, who ordered him to bow. Wenxiu said, "We are ministers of two states alike—why should I bow!"

sentences.zh: 白曜還其衣，為之設饌，鎖送平城。

translations.literal: Baiyao returned his clothes, set out food for him, and under lock sent him to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao restored his clothes, set food before him, and sent him under guard to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 魏主數其罪而宥之，待為下客，給惡衣、疏食；

translations.literal: The Wei ruler enumerated his crimes yet pardoned him, treated him as a lower guest, and gave him poor clothes and coarse food;
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor listed his crimes yet spared him, treated him as an inferior guest, and gave him poor clothes and coarse food;

sentences.zh: 既而重其不屈，稍嘉禮之，拜外都下大夫。

translations.literal: afterward, valuing his refusal to yield, he gradually honored him with courtesy and appointed him Outer Metropolitan Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: then, respecting his unyielding spirit, gradually honored him and appointed him Outer Metropolitan Grandee.

sentences.zh: 於是青、冀之地盡入於魏矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon the lands of Qing and Ji all entered Wei.
translations.idiomatic: With that, the lands of Qing and Ji passed entirely to Wei.

sentences.zh: 二月，己卯，魏以慕容白曜為都督青、齊、東徐三州諸軍事、征南大將軍、開府儀同三司、青州刺史，進爵濟南王。

translations.literal: In the second month, on jimao, Wei made Murong Baiyao Commander-in-Chief of the Military Affairs of the three provinces Qing, Qi, and Eastern Xu, General-in-Chief Who Conquers the South, Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, regional inspector of Qingzhou, and advanced his rank to Prince of Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on jimao Wei appointed Murong Baiyao commander of military affairs in Qing, Qi, and Eastern Xu, General-in-Chief Who Conquers the South, Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, inspector of Qingzhou, and raised him to Prince of Jinan.

sentences.zh: 白曜撫御有方，東人安之。

translations.literal: Baiyao governed and controlled with method; the eastern people were at peace under him.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao governed wisely and the eastern people lived in peace under him.

sentences.zh: 魏自天安以來，比歲旱饑，重以青、徐用兵，山東之民疲於賦役。

translations.literal: Wei since the Tian'an era, year after year had drought and famine; added to this was military use in Qing and Xu—the people of Shandong were exhausted by taxes and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Tian'an era Wei had suffered drought and famine year after year; war in Qing and Xu added to the burden, and the people of Shandong were worn out by taxes and labor.

sentences.zh: 顯祖命因民貧富，為三等輸租之法，等為三品：上三品輸平城，中輸它州，下輸本州。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu ordered that according to the people's wealth and poverty a law of three grades for delivering rent be made; the grades were three classes: the upper three classes delivered to Pingcheng, the middle delivered to other provinces, the lower delivered to their own province.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzu ordered rent graded by wealth into three classes: the wealthiest paid to Pingcheng, the middle rank to other provinces, the poorest to their home province.

sentences.zh: 又，魏舊制：常賦之外，有雜調十五；

translations.literal: Moreover, Wei's old system: beyond the regular levy there were fifteen miscellaneous exactions;
translations.idiomatic: Wei also abolished the fifteen miscellaneous levies beyond the regular tax;

sentences.zh: 至是悉罷之，由是民稍贍給。

translations.literal: at this time all were abolished, and thereby the people gradually had enough to live.
translations.idiomatic: and the people gradually recovered their livelihood.

sentences.zh: 河東柳欣慰等謀反，欲立太尉廬江王禕。

translations.literal: Liu Xinwei of Hedong and others plotted rebellion, wishing to establish the Grand Marshal, the Prince of Lujiang Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xinwei of Hedong and others plotted rebellion, intending to set up Grand Marshal Prince of Lujiang Yi.

sentences.zh: 禕自以於帝為兄，而帝及諸兄弟皆輕之，遂與欣慰等通謀相酬和。

translations.literal: Yi considered himself the emperor's elder brother, yet the emperor and all the brothers alike slighted him; he therefore communicated in conspiracy with Xinwei and the others, responding to one another.
translations.idiomatic: Yi considered himself the emperor's elder brother, yet the emperor and his brothers all slighted him; he therefore conspired with Xinwei and his fellows.

sentences.zh: 征北咨議參軍杜幼文告之，丙申，詔降禕為車騎將軍、開府儀同三司、南豫州刺史，出鎮宣城，帝遣腹心楊運長領兵防衛。

translations.literal: Du Youwen, Consulting Staff Officer of the Army of the North, reported it; on bingshen an edict demoted Yi to General of Chariots and Cavalry, Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, regional inspector of Southern Yuzhou, sent out to garrison Xuancheng; the emperor dispatched his trusted man Yang Yunchang to lead troops to guard and defend.
translations.idiomatic: Consulting staff officer Du Youwen of the Army of the North reported the plot; on bingshen an edict demoted Yi to General of Chariots and Cavalry, Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and inspector of Southern Yuzhou, sent to garrison Xuancheng under guard of the emperor's favorite Yang Yunchang.

sentences.zh: 欣慰等並伏誅。

translations.literal: Xinwei and the others all were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Xinwei and the others were all executed.

sentences.zh: 三月，魏人寇汝陰，太守楊文萇擊卻之。

translations.literal: In the third month, Wei forces raided Ruyin; Grand Administrator Yang Wenchang struck and drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Northern Wei troops attacked Ruyin, but Grand Administrator Yang Wenchang repelled them.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丙申，魏大赦。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on bingshen, Wei proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, on the bingshen day of the fourth month, Northern Wei issued a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 五月，魏徙青、齊民於平城，置升城、歷城民望於桑干，立平齊郡以居之；

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Wei relocated the people of Qing and Qi to Pingcheng, settled the leading families of Shengcheng and Licheng at Sanggan, and established Pingqi Commandery to house them;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Northern Wei moved the populace of Qing and Qi to Pingcheng, resettled the leading families of Shengcheng and Licheng along the Sanggan River, and created Pingqi Commandery to receive them;

sentences.zh: 自餘悉為奴婢，分賜百官。

translations.literal: all the rest were made slaves and servants and distributed as gifts to the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: the remainder were all reduced to bondage and parceled out as gifts to officials throughout the court.

sentences.zh: 魏沙門統曇曜奏：「平齊戶及諸民有能歲輸谷六十斛入僧曹者，即為僧祇戶，粟為僧祇粟，遇凶歲，賑給饑民。」

translations.literal: The Wei Superintendent of Buddhist Clergy, Tanyao, memorialized: "Among the Pingqi households and other people, those able each year to deliver sixty hu of grain to the monastic office shall be made sangha-treasury households, and the grain shall be sangha-treasury grain; in years of famine it shall be distributed to relieve the hungry."
translations.idiomatic: Tanyao, Northern Wei's superintendent of the Buddhist clergy, submitted a memorial: "Let any household from the relocated Pingqi population or elsewhere that can pay sixty hu of grain annually into the monastic treasury be registered as a sangha-treasury household; that grain shall be held as sangha reserve grain and, in years of dearth, used to feed the starving."

sentences.zh: 又請：「民犯重罪及官奴，以為佛圖戶，以供諸寺掃灑。」

translations.literal: He further requested: "Commoners guilty of grave crimes and government slaves shall be made Buddha-households to supply sweeping and cleaning for the various monasteries."
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that "criminals convicted of serious offenses, together with official slaves, be assigned as Buddha-households to perform menial labor for the temples."

sentences.zh: 魏主並許之。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler approved both requests.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor granted both proposals.

sentences.zh: 於是僧祇戶、粟及寺戶遍於州鎮矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon sangha-treasury households, sangha grain, and monastery households spread throughout the provinces and garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: From that point on, sangha-treasury households, reserve grain, and temple bondsmen appeared in garrisons and provinces across the realm.

sentences.zh: 六月，魏立皇子宏為太子。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Wei established the imperial son Hong as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Northern Wei named the emperor's son Hong crown prince.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，以左衛將軍沈攸之為郢州刺史。

translations.literal: On guiyou, Left Guard General Shen Youzhi was made regional inspector of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, Left Guard General Shen Youzhi was appointed inspector of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 上又令有司奏廬江王禕忿懟有怨言，請窮治；

translations.literal: The emperor again ordered the relevant offices to memorialize that the Prince of Lujiang, Yi, in resentment and anger had uttered complaints, and to request a thorough investigation;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again had the authorities report that Prince of Lujiang Yi, embittered and resentful, had spoken words of complaint, and ask that the matter be pursued to the end;

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: he refused.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，免禕官爵，遣大鴻臚持節奉詔責禕，因逼令自殺，子輔國將軍充明廢徙新安。

translations.literal: On dingchou, Yi was stripped of office and rank; the Grand Herald was dispatched bearing the staff of authority to deliver an imperial reprimand to Yi and thereby compel him to take his own life; his son, General Who Assists the State Chongming, was deposed and banished to Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou, Yi was stripped of rank and title; the Grand Herald was sent with imperial credentials to rebuke him and force him to commit suicide, while his son Chongming, a general who assists the state, was removed from office and exiled to Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丁卯朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on dingmao, the first day of the month, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, on the first day of the tenth month, dingmao, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 魏頓丘王李峻卒。

translations.literal: Li Jun, Prince of Dunqiu of Wei, died.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jun, Prince of Dunqiu in Northern Wei, died.

sentences.zh: 十一月，丁未，魏復遣使來修和親，自是信使歲通。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on dingwei, Wei again sent envoys to renew matrimonial alliance; from this time diplomatic messengers passed back and forth every year.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on dingwei, Northern Wei once again sent envoys to restore friendly relations, and thereafter diplomatic couriers traveled between the two courts every year.

sentences.zh: 閏月，戊子，以輔師將軍猛陽為兗州刺史，始治淮陰。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on wuzi, General Who Assists the Army Meng Yang was made regional inspector of Yanzhou and for the first time administered from Huaiyin.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on wuzi, General Who Assists the Army Meng Yang was appointed inspector of Yanzhou and established his seat at Huaiyin for the first time.

sentences.zh: 十二月，戊戌，司徒建安王休仁解揚州。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on wuxu, Grand Marshal Prince of Jian'an Xiuren relinquished Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on wuxu, Grand Marshal Prince of Jian'an Xiuren resigned his post as inspector of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 休仁年與上鄰亞，素相友愛，景和之世，上賴其力以脫禍。

translations.literal: Xiuren's age was close to the emperor's, and they had long been friendly and affectionate; in the Jinghe era the emperor relied on his strength to escape disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuren was nearly the emperor's age and had long been on close, affectionate terms with him; during the Jinghe reign the emperor had depended on him to survive the crisis.

sentences.zh: 及泰始初，四方兵起，休仁親當矢石，克成大功，任總百揆，親寄甚隆；

translations.literal: When Taishi began, warfare arose on all sides; Xiuren personally faced arrows and stones, achieved great merit, held overall charge of all affairs of state, and enjoyed exceedingly lofty imperial trust;
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Taishi era, when rebellion flared on every side, Xiuren had personally braved battle, won great victories, and come to oversee the whole government, enjoying the emperor's deepest trust;

sentences.zh: 由是朝野輻湊，上漸不悅。

translations.literal: because of this court and countryside converged upon him, and the emperor gradually became displeased.
translations.idiomatic: as a result, officials and commoners alike flocked to him, and the emperor slowly grew uneasy.

sentences.zh: 休仁悟其旨，故表解揚州。

translations.literal: Xiuren understood his intent and therefore submitted a memorial relinquishing Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Reading the emperor's mind, Xiuren petitioned to surrender the Yangzhou post.

sentences.zh: 己未，以桂陽王休范為揚州刺史。

translations.literal: On jiwei, Prince of Guiyang Xiufan was made regional inspector of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, Prince of Guiyang Xiufan was appointed inspector of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 分荊州之巴東、建平，益州之巴西、梓潼郡，置三巴校尉，治白帝。

translations.literal: The commanderies of Badong and Jianping in Jingzhou and Brazil and Zitong in Yizhou were separated off and a Commandant of the Three Ba was established, with his seat at Baidi.
translations.idiomatic: Badong and Jianping in Jingzhou together with Brazil and Zitong in Yizhou were carved out to form a Three Ba commandery, headed by a commandant stationed at Baidi.

sentences.zh: 先是，三峽蠻、獠歲為抄暴，故立府以鎮之。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Man and Liao of the Three Gorges had raided and plundered year after year; therefore this office was established to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: The post had been created because the tribal peoples of the Three Gorges had been raiding the region year after year.

sentences.zh: 上以司徒參軍東莞孫謙為巴東、建平二郡太守。

translations.literal: The emperor appointed Sun Qian of Dongguan, a staff officer to the Grand Marshal, grand administrator of the two commanderies of Badong and Jianping.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor named Sun Qian of Dongguan, an aide on the grand marshal's staff, administrator of the twin commanderies of Badong and Jianping.

sentences.zh: 謙將之官，敕募千人自隨，謙曰：「亦夷不賓，蓋待之失節耳，何煩兵役以為國費！」

translations.literal: When Qian was about to take up his post, an edict ordered him to raise a thousand men to accompany him; Qian said: "When barbarians do not submit, it is generally because they have been treated without proper measure—why trouble military service and burden the state's expense!"
translations.idiomatic: As Qian prepared to take office, the court ordered him to raise a thousand troops for his escort, but he replied: "When tribes refuse allegiance, it is usually because we have failed them in courtesy—why waste soldiers and drain the treasury on account of it!"

sentences.zh: 固辭不受。

translations.literal: He firmly declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He steadfastly refused.

sentences.zh: 至郡，開布恩信，蠻、獠翕然懷之，競餉金寶；

translations.literal: On reaching the commandery, he openly spread favor and good faith; the Man and Liao all at once turned to him in affection and vied to present gold and precious objects;
translations.idiomatic: Once in office, he governed with openness and trust, and the tribal peoples quickly warmed to him, competing to bring him gifts of gold and jewels;

sentences.zh: 謙皆慰諭，不受。

translations.literal: Qian in every case comforted and instructed them and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Qian thanked them kindly each time and declined every gift.

sentences.zh: 臨海賊帥田流自稱東海王，剽掠海鹽，殺鄞令，東土大震。

translations.literal: Tian Liu, bandit chieftain of Linhai, styled himself King of the Eastern Sea, plundered coastal salt, killed the magistrate of Yin, and greatly shook the eastern lands.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Liu, a bandit leader in Linhai, proclaimed himself King of the Eastern Sea, raided the coastal salt trade, murdered the magistrate of Yin, and threw the eastern provinces into alarm.

sentences.zh: 太宗明皇帝中泰始六年（

translations.literal: Sixth year of Taishi of Emperor Ming the Filial and Bright (
translations.idiomatic: The sixth year of Taishi under Emperor Ming the Filial and Bright (

sentences.zh: 庚戌，公元四七零年）

translations.literal: gengxu, CE 470)
translations.idiomatic: gengxu, 470 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙亥，初制間二年一祭南郊，間一年一祭明堂。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on yihai, for the first time a rule was established: every other year sacrifice at the Southern Suburb, every other year sacrifice at the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on yihai, the first day of the first month, a new schedule was set: sacrifices at the Southern Altar every two years and at the Bright Hall in the intervening years.

sentences.zh: 二月，壬寅，以司徒休仁為太尉，領司徒；

translations.literal: In the second month, on renyin, Grand Marshal Xiuren was made Grand Commandant and concurrently held the post of Grand Marshal;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on renyin, Grand Marshal Xiuren was promoted to grand commandant while retaining the grand marshalship;

sentences.zh: 固辭。

translations.literal: he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: he firmly declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，納江智淵孫女為太子妃。

translations.literal: On guichou, the granddaughter of Jiang Zhiyuan was taken in as crown princess.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, the crown prince wed the granddaughter of Jiang Zhiyuan.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，大赦。

translations.literal: On jiayin, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, the court proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 令百官皆獻物；

translations.literal: All hundred officials were ordered to present gifts;
translations.idiomatic: All officials were ordered to present tribute gifts;

sentences.zh: 始興太守孫奉伯止獻琴、書，上大怒，封藥賜死，既而原之。

translations.literal: Sun Fengbo, grand administrator of Shixing, presented only a zither and books; the emperor was greatly enraged, sealed medicine and bestowed death, but afterward pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fengbo, administrator of Shixing, offered only a zither and some books; the emperor flew into a rage and sent sealed poison with orders that he die, but later relented and spared him.

sentences.zh: 魏以東郡王陸定國為司空。

translations.literal: Wei made Lu Dingguo, Prince of the Eastern Region, Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei appointed Lu Dingguo, Prince of the Eastern Region, minister of works.

sentences.zh: 定國，麗之子也。

translations.literal: Dingguo was the son of Li.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo was a son of Li.

sentences.zh: 魏主遣征西大將軍上黨王長孫觀擊吐谷渾。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler dispatched Campaigning Western Grand General Changsun Guan, Prince of Shangdang, to attack Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor sent Campaigning Western Grand General Changsun Guan, Prince of Shangdang, against Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，辛丑，魏大赦。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on xinchou, Wei proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, on the xinchou day of the fourth month, Northern Wei issued a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 戊申，魏長孫觀與葉欲渾王拾寅戰於曼頭山，拾寅敗走，遣別駕康盤龍入貢，魏主囚之。

translations.literal: On wushen, Changsun Guan of Wei fought with Shibin, king of Tuyuhun, at Mantou Mountain; Shibin was defeated and fled, sent his aide Kang Panlong to enter with tribute, and the Wei ruler imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, Changsun Guan of Northern Wei battled Tuyuhun King Shibin at Mantou Mountain; Shibin was routed and fled, then sent his aide Kang Panlong with tribute, but the Wei emperor had him detained.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，立皇子燮為晉熙王，奉晉熙王昶後。

translations.literal: On guihai, the imperial son Xie was established as Prince of Jinxi to continue the line of Prince of Jinxi Chang.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, the emperor's son Xie was enfeoffed as Prince of Jinxi to carry on the house of the former Prince of Jinxi Chang.

sentences.zh: 五月，魏立皇弟長樂為建昌王。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Wei established the emperor's younger brother Changle as Prince of Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Northern Wei enfeoffed the emperor's younger brother Changle as Prince of Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 六月，癸卯，以江州刺史王景文為尚書左僕射、揚州刺史，以尚書僕射袁粲為右僕射。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on guimao, Wang Jingwen, regional inspector of Jiangzhou, was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and regional inspector of Yangzhou, and Yuan Can, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was made Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on guimao, Wang Jingwen, inspector of Jiangzhou, was appointed left vice director of the Masters of Writing and inspector of Yangzhou, while Yuan Can, vice director of the Masters of Writing, became right vice director.

sentences.zh: 上宮中大宴，裸婦人而觀之，王后以戶扇障面。

translations.literal: The emperor held a great banquet in the palace, had naked women for viewing, and the empress screened her face with a door fan.
translations.idiomatic: At a grand palace feast the emperor set naked women on display for amusement, and the empress hid her face behind a door screen.

sentences.zh: 上怒曰：「外捨寒乞！

translations.literal: The emperor angrily said: "Outsiders and cold beggars!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor snapped in anger: "You in-laws are nothing but paupers from outside!

sentences.zh: 今共為樂，何獨不視！」

translations.literal: Now we share in pleasure together—why alone do you not look!"
translations.idiomatic: We are all here to enjoy ourselves—why won't you look like everyone else!"

sentences.zh: 後曰：「為樂之事，其方自多；

translations.literal: The empress said: "Matters of pleasure have many proper ways;
translations.idiomatic: The empress replied: "There are many ways to take one's pleasure;

sentences.zh: 豈有姑姊妹集，而裸婦人以為笑！

translations.literal: how can there be a gathering of aunts and sisters with naked women held up for laughter!
translations.idiomatic: surely it is not fitting for aunts and sisters to gather while naked women are put on display for sport!

sentences.zh: 外捨之樂，雅異於此。」

translations.literal: The pleasures of outsiders' households are elegantly different from this."
translations.idiomatic: The diversions of an outsider's household are quite unlike this."

sentences.zh: 上大怒，遣後起。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged and sent the empress away.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and had the empress dismissed from the hall.

sentences.zh: 後兄景文聞之，曰：「後在家劣弱，今段遂能剛正如此！」

translations.literal: When the empress's elder brother Jingwen heard of it, he said: "The empress at home was weak and yielding; in this affair she was able to be so upright and firm!"
translations.idiomatic: When the empress's brother Jingwen heard what had happened, he said: "At home she was always meek and mild—who would have thought she could stand up to him like this!"

sentences.zh: 南兗州刺史蕭道成在軍中久，民間或言道成有異相，當為天子。

translations.literal: Xiao Daocheng, regional inspector of Southern Yanzhou, had long been in the army; among the people some said Daocheng had an unusual physiognomy and would become Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Daocheng, inspector of Southern Yanzhou, had been in the field for a long time, and among the people there were whispers that he bore the marks of emperorship and was destined to rule.

sentences.zh: 上疑之，征為黃門侍郎、越騎校尉。

translations.literal: The emperor grew suspicious and summoned him to serve as Gentleman at the Yellow Gate and Commandant of the Rapid Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew suspicious and recalled him to court as gentleman at the yellow gate and commandant of the rapid cavalry.

sentences.zh: 道成懼，不欲內遷，而無計得留。

translations.literal: Daocheng was afraid and did not wish to move inward, yet had no stratagem by which to remain.
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng was alarmed; he did not want to be pulled back to the capital, but he could see no way to stay where he was.

sentences.zh: 冠軍參軍廣陵荀伯玉勸道成遣數十騎入魏境，安置標榜，魏果遣游騎數百履行境上；

translations.literal: Xun Boyu of Guangling, army aide to the Champion General, advised Daocheng to send several dozen horsemen into Wei territory to set up placards; Wei indeed sent several hundred patrol horsemen to traverse the border;
translations.idiomatic: Xun Boyu of Guangling, an aide on Daocheng's staff, urged him to send a few dozen horsemen into Wei territory to plant boundary markers, and Wei promptly dispatched hundreds of patrol riders to ride the frontier;

sentences.zh: 道成以聞，上使道成復本任。

translations.literal: Daocheng reported this, and the emperor had Daocheng return to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng reported the incursion, and the emperor sent him back to his original command.

sentences.zh: 秋，九月，命道成遷鎮淮陰。

translations.literal: In autumn, the ninth month, Daocheng was ordered to transfer his garrison to Huaiyin.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the ninth month, Daocheng was ordered to shift his headquarters to Huaiyin.

sentences.zh: 以侍中、中領軍劉勉為都督南徐、兗等五州諸軍事，鎮廣陵。

translations.literal: Liu Mian, Palace Attendant and Central Army Commander, was made area commander of military affairs for five provinces including Southern Xu and Yan, garrisoning at Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mian, palace attendant and central army commander, was made area commander over five provinces including Southern Xu and Yan, with his seat at Guangling.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，立總明觀，置祭酒一人，儒、玄、文、史學士各十人。

translations.literal: On wuyin, the Zongming Observatory was established, with one libationer appointed and ten scholars each in Confucian, Dark Learning, literary, and historical studies.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, the court founded the Zongming Observatory, appointing one libationer and ten scholars each in Confucian, Daoist, literary, and historical learning.

sentences.zh: 柔然部真可汗侵魏，魏主引郡臣議之。

translations.literal: Buyegu Khan of Rouran invaded Wei, and the Wei ruler summoned the court ministers to discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: Buyegu Khan of the Rouran invaded Northern Wei, and the emperor convened his ministers to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 尚書右僕射南平公目辰日：「若車駕親征，京師危懼，不如持重固守。

translations.literal: Mu Chen, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Duke of Nanping, said: "If the imperial carriage goes on campaign in person, the capital will be endangered and fearful; it is better to hold firm and defend with weight.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Chen, right vice director of the Masters of Writing and Duke of Nanping, argued: "If Your Majesty leads the campaign in person, the capital will be left exposed and terrified; it would be safer to hold the city and wait.

sentences.zh: 虜懸軍深入，糧運無繼，不久自退；

translations.literal: The barbarians have left their base and advanced deep; their grain transport cannot be sustained—they will before long withdraw of themselves;
translations.idiomatic: The enemy has marched deep with no secure supply line; before long they will withdraw on their own;

sentences.zh: 遣將追擊，破之必矣。」

translations.literal: send generals in pursuit to strike them, and crushing them is certain."
translations.idiomatic: then we can send generals in pursuit and crush them with certainty."

sentences.zh: 給事中張白澤曰：「蠢爾荒愚，輕犯王略，若鑾輿親行，必望麾崩散，豈可坐而縱敵！

translations.literal: Supervising Gentleman Zhang Baize said: "Stupid and wild in their ignorance, they lightly violate the royal domain; if the imperial palanquin goes in person, they will surely look to the banner and scatter in collapse—how can one sit and let the enemy go!
translations.idiomatic: Supervising gentleman Zhang Baize countered: "These crude barbarians have rashly violated the imperial domain; if Your Majesty marches in person, they will break and flee at the sight of the imperial standard—how can we sit idle and let them escape!

sentences.zh: 以萬乘之尊，嬰城自守，非所以威服四夷也。」

translations.literal: With the dignity of ten thousand chariots, to cling to the city and defend oneself is not the way to awe and subdue the four barbarians."
translations.idiomatic: For the sovereign of an empire to cower behind city walls is no way to overawe the peoples of the four directions."

sentences.zh: 魏主從之。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor accepted his counsel.

sentences.zh: 白澤，袞之孫也。

translations.literal: Baize was the grandson of Gun.
translations.idiomatic: Baize was a grandson of Gun.

sentences.zh: 魏主使京兆王子推等督諸軍出西道，任城王雲等督諸軍出東道，汝陰王天賜等督諸軍為前鋒，隴西王源賀等督諸軍為後斷，鎮西將軍呂羅漢等掌留台事。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler had Wang Zitui of Jingzhao and others supervise the armies on the western route, Prince of Rencheng Yun and others supervise the armies on the eastern route, Prince of Ruyin Tianci and others supervise the armies as vanguard, Wang Yuanhe of Longxi and others supervise the armies as rear guard, and General Who Pacifies the West Lü Luohan and others manage affairs of the capital in the ruler's absence.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Wang Zitui of Jingzhao and others to command the western column, Prince of Rencheng Yun and others the eastern column, Prince of Ruyin Tianci and others the vanguard, Wang Yuanhe of Longxi and others the rearguard, and General Who Pacifies the West Lü Luohan and others to govern the capital in his absence.

sentences.zh: 諸將會魏主於女水之濱，與柔然戰，柔然大敗。

translations.literal: The generals joined the Wei ruler on the banks of the Nü River and fought with Rouran; Rouran was greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The commanders rendezvoused with the emperor on the banks of the Nü River, gave battle to the Rouran, and routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 乘勝逐北，斬首五萬級，降者萬餘人，猶戎馬器械不可勝計。

translations.literal: Riding the victory they pursued north; heads cut numbered fifty thousand, those who surrendered more than ten thousand, and besides that war horses and weapons were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing the pursuit, they took fifty thousand heads, accepted more than ten thousand surrenders, and captured horses and arms beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 旬有九日，往返六千餘里。

translations.literal: In nineteen days they went out and returned more than six thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: The entire campaign lasted nineteen days and covered more than six thousand li there and back.

sentences.zh: 改女水曰武川。

translations.literal: The Nü River was renamed Wuchuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Nü River was renamed the Wuchuan.

sentences.zh: 司徒東安王劉尼坐昏醉，軍陳不整，免官。

translations.literal: Liu Ni, Prince of Dong'an and Grand Marshal, was punished because, drunk and befuddled, his battle array was not orderly; he was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Liu Ni, Prince of Dong'an, was dismissed for taking the field while drunk and leaving his ranks in disorder.

sentences.zh: 壬申，還至平城。

translations.literal: On renshen, he returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, the emperor returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 是時，魏百官不給祿，少能以廉白自立者。

translations.literal: At this time, the hundred officials of Wei received no salaries, and few were able to establish themselves in integrity and purity.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Northern Wei's officials received no salaries, and few could remain honest on their own.

sentences.zh: 魏主詔：「吏受所監臨羊一口、酒一斛者，死；

translations.literal: The Wei ruler decreed: "Officials who receive from those they supervise one sheep or one hu of wine shall die;
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor issued an edict: "Any official who accepts so much as one sheep or one hu of wine from those under his supervision shall be put to death;

sentences.zh: 與者以從坐論。

translations.literal: those who give shall be judged as accomplices.
translations.idiomatic: those who offer such gifts shall be punished as accomplices.

sentences.zh: 有能糾告尚書已下罪狀者，隨所糾官輕重授之。」

translations.literal: Those able to impeach and report crimes of officials from Masters of Writing downward shall be given appointment according to the lighter or heavier rank of the official impeached."
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who exposed wrongdoing by an official of vice-director rank or below would be promoted to fill the vacant post, commensurate with the offender's rank."

sentences.zh: 張白澤諫曰：「昔周之下士，尚有代耕之祿。

translations.literal: Zhang Baize remonstrated: "In former times even the lower officers of Zhou still had salaries in lieu of farming.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Baize remonstrated: "Even the lowest officers of the Zhou received grain salaries in lieu of farming.

sentences.zh: 今皇朝貴臣，服勤無報；

translations.literal: Now the honored ministers of the imperial court serve diligently yet receive no reward;
translations.idiomatic: Today the empire's highest ministers serve without compensation;

sentences.zh: 若使受禮者刑身，糾之者代職，臣恐奸人窺望，忠臣懈節，如此而求事簡民安，不亦難乎！

translations.literal: if those who accept gifts are punished in body and those who impeach replace them in office, I fear wicked men will watch and wait while loyal ministers relax their integrity—seeking simplified affairs and a tranquil people in this way, is it not also difficult!
translations.idiomatic: if accepting a gift means death and denouncing a colleague means taking his post, I fear schemers will watch for openings while honest men lose heart; under such conditions, how can government be kept simple and the people kept at peace!

sentences.zh: 請依律令舊法，仍班祿以酬廉吏。」

translations.literal: I request that according to the statutes and former laws, salaries again be distributed to reward upright officials."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the old statutes be restored and salaries paid again to reward upright service."

sentences.zh: 魏主乃為之罷新法。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler thereupon abolished the new law on his account.
translations.idiomatic: On his advice, the Wei emperor revoked the new measure.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，辛卯，詔以世祖繼體，陷憲無遺，以皇子智隨為世祖子，立為武陵王。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on xinmao, an edict declared that because Emperor Shizu had continued the imperial line and left no descendant unprovided for, the imperial son Zhisui was made a son of Emperor Shizu and established as Prince of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, on xinmao in the tenth month, an edict declared that because Emperor Shizu had continued the dynastic line and no descendant of his should be left without heirs, the emperor's son Zhisui was adopted as Shizu's son and enfeoffed as Prince of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 初，魏乙渾專政，慕容白曜頗附之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yi Hun monopolized government in Wei, Murong Baiyao had largely attached himself to him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Yi Hun had dominated the Wei court, Murong Baiyao had closely aligned himself with him.

sentences.zh: 魏主追以為憾，遂稱白曜謀反，誅之，及其弟如意。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler afterward considered this a regret and therefore declared that Baiyao had plotted rebellion, executed him, and also his younger brother Ruyi.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor still resented that association and therefore charged Baiyao with treason, executed him, and put his younger brother Ruyi to death as well.

sentences.zh: 初，魏南部尚書李敷，儀曹尚書李言斤，少相親善，與中書侍郎盧度世皆以才能為世祖、顯祖所寵任，參豫機密，出納詔命。

translations.literal: Earlier, Li Fu of Wei, Minister of the Southern Branch, and Li Yanjin, Minister of the Bureau of Rites, had from youth been close and friendly; together with Secretariat Gentleman Lu Dushi they all, by their talent, were favored and entrusted by Emperor Shizu and Emperor Xianzu, took part in secret affairs, and issued and received imperial edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Li Fu, minister of the southern branch, and Li Yanjin, minister of the bureau of rites, had been close friends since youth; they and Secretariat Gentleman Lu Dushi, all men of proven ability, had been favored by Emperors Shizu and Xianzu, entrusted with state secrets, and charged with drafting and transmitting imperial orders.

sentences.zh: 其後言斤出為相州刺史，受納貨賂，為人所告，敷掩蔽之。

translations.literal: Afterward Yanjin went out as regional inspector of Xiangzhou, accepted bribes, was reported by others, and Fu concealed it.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yanjin was sent out as inspector of Xiangzhou, where he took bribes; when someone reported him, Fu covered up the offense.

sentences.zh: 顯祖聞之，檻車征言斤，案驗服罪，當死。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzu heard of it, he summoned Yanjin in a caged cart; investigation verified the guilt, and death was the proper penalty.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzu learned of it, he had Yanjin brought back in a prison cart; the inquiry confirmed his guilt, and the sentence was death.

sentences.zh: 是時敷弟弈得幸於馮太后，帝意已疏之。

translations.literal: At this time Fu's younger brother Yi had gained favor with Empress Dowager Feng, and the emperor's mind had already grown distant toward them.
translations.idiomatic: By then Fu's younger brother Yi had won favor with Empress Dowager Feng, and the emperor had already begun to keep his distance from the family.

sentences.zh: 有司以中旨諷言斤告敷兄弟陰事，可以得免。

translations.literal: The relevant offices, by an inner directive, hinted to Yanjin that if he reported the hidden affairs of Fu and his brothers, he could be spared.
translations.idiomatic: On a hint from the palace, the authorities suggested to Yanjin that if he denounced the Fu brothers' secret crimes, he might escape punishment.

sentences.zh: 言斤謂其婿裴攸曰：「吾與敷族世雖遠，恩逾同生，今在事勸吾為此，吾情所不忍。

translations.literal: Yanjin said to his son-in-law Pei You: "Although Fu and I are distant in clan generation, our kindness exceeds that of brothers born together; now those handling the case urge me to do this—I cannot bear it in my feelings.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjin told his son-in-law Pei You: "Though Fu and I are only distant kinsmen, our bond is closer than that of brothers; now the officials urge me to betray him, and my heart will not allow it.

sentences.zh: 每引簪自刺，解帶自絞，終不得死。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he drew his hairpin to stab himself and loosened his belt to strangle himself, yet in the end could not die.
translations.idiomatic: Again and again he tried to stab himself with his hairpin or hang himself with his belt, but he could not succeed in dying.

sentences.zh: 且吾安能知其陰事！

translations.literal: Moreover, how could I know their hidden affairs!
translations.idiomatic: Besides, how would I even know their secret crimes!

sentences.zh: 將若之何？」

translations.literal: What is to be done about it?"
translations.idiomatic: What can be done?"

sentences.zh: 攸曰：「何為為人死也！

translations.literal: You said, "Why die for another!
translations.idiomatic: Pei You said, "Why die for someone else!

sentences.zh: 有馮闡者，先為敷所敗，其家深怨之。

translations.literal: There was one Feng Chan who had earlier been defeated by Fu; his family deeply resented him.
translations.idiomatic: There was a man named Feng Chan whom Fu had once defeated; his family bore a deep grudge.

sentences.zh: 今詢其弟，敷之陰事可得也。」

translations.literal: If we now inquire of his younger brother, Fu's secret affairs can be obtained."
translations.idiomatic: Question his younger brother now and we can obtain Fu's hidden crimes."

sentences.zh: 言斤從之。

translations.literal: Yanjin followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjin took his advice.

sentences.zh: 又趙郡范檦條列敷兄弟事狀凡三十餘條。

translations.literal: Moreover Fan Biao of Zhao Commandery itemized the affairs of Fu and his brothers in more than thirty articles.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Biao of Zhao Commandery also listed more than thirty charges against Fu and his brothers.

sentences.zh: 有司以聞，帝大怒，誅敷兄弟。

translations.literal: The responsible officials reported it; the emperor was greatly angry and executed Fu and his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities reported this to the throne; the emperor flew into a rage and executed Fu and his brothers.

sentences.zh: 言斤得減死，鞭髡配役。

translations.literal: Yanjin had his death reduced, was flogged, shaved, and assigned to corvée service.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjin escaped death but was flogged, shorn, and sentenced to penal labor.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復為太倉尚書，攝南部事。

translations.literal: Before long he was again made Minister of the Grand Granary, acting for southern-branch affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was restored as Minister of the Grand Granary with acting charge of the southern branch.

sentences.zh: 敷，順之子也。

translations.literal: Fu was the son of Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was a son of Li Shun.

sentences.zh: 魏陽平王新成卒。

translations.literal: Wei's Prince of Yangping, Xincheng, died.
translations.idiomatic: Xincheng, Prince of Yangping of Wei, died.

sentences.zh: 是歲，命龍驤將軍義興周山圖將兵屯浹口討田流，平之。

translations.literal: In this year the Dragon Cavalry General Zhou Shantu of Yixing was ordered to lead troops to encamp at Jiakou to attack Tian Liu and pacify him.
translations.idiomatic: That year Dragon Cavalry General Zhou Shantu of Yixing was ordered to camp at Jiakou against Tian Liu and pacified the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 柔然攻于闐，于闐遣使者素目伽奉表詣魏求救。

translations.literal: Rouran attacked Yutian; Yutian sent the envoy Sumujia to present a memorial to Wei seeking rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Rouran attacked Yutian; Yutian sent the envoy Sumujia with a memorial to Wei begging for aid.

sentences.zh: 魏主命公卿議之，畢曰：「于闐去京師幾萬里，蠕蠕唯習野掠，不能攻城；

translations.literal: The Wei ruler ordered the dukes and ministers to deliberate. Bi said, "Yutian is tens of thousands of li from the capital; the Rouran are skilled only in wild raiding and cannot besiege cities;
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor ordered his ministers to debate the matter. Bi said, "Yutian lies tens of thousands of li from the capital; the Rouran know only raiding in the open country and cannot take walled cities;

sentences.zh: 若其可攻，尋已亡矣。

translations.literal: if it could be attacked, it would long since have perished.
translations.idiomatic: if they could storm it, the kingdom would already be gone.

sentences.zh: 雖欲遣師，勢無所及。」

translations.literal: Even if we wished to send an army, our strength could not reach there."
translations.idiomatic: Even if we wished to send troops, we could not reach them in time."

sentences.zh: 魏主以議示使者，使者亦以為然。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler showed the deliberation to the envoy, and the envoy also thought it so.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor showed the deliberation to the envoy, who agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃詔之曰：「朕應仇敕諸軍以拯汝難。

translations.literal: He thereupon addressed him with an edict, saying, "We, in response to enmity, shall command the armies to save you from calamity.
translations.idiomatic: He then told him by edict, "We shall command our armies to answer your call and deliver you from disaster.

sentences.zh: 但去汝遐阻，必不能救當時之急，汝宜知之。

translations.literal: But the distance to you is vast and obstructed; we surely cannot save the urgency of the moment—you should know this.
translations.idiomatic: But you are far away, and we cannot relieve your immediate peril—you must understand this.

sentences.zh: 朕今練甲養士，一二歲間，當躬帥猛將，為汝除患。

translations.literal: We now drill armor and nurture soldiers; within a year or two we shall personally lead fierce generals to remove your affliction for you.
translations.idiomatic: We are now training troops; within a year or two we shall lead our best generals in person to destroy your enemy.

sentences.zh: 汝其謹修警候，以待大舉。」

translations.literal: You should carefully maintain watch and guard, and await the great campaign."
translations.idiomatic: Keep your defenses in order and await our great expedition."
